L320: ## 6.2.2. Study 200808/ASCEND-ND
L321: ## 6.2.2.1. Design
L322: ## Overview
L323: To support an indication for the treatment of anemia due to CKD in patients not on dialysis, the Applicant conducted a randomized, Phase 3 Study, 200808/ASCEND-ND, titled “A phase 3 randomized, open-label (sponsor-blind), active controlled, parallel-group, multi-center, event driven study in non-dialysis subjects with anemia associated with chronic kidney disease to evaluate the safety and efficacy of daprodustat compared to darbepoetin alfa.”
L324: ## Primary Safety and Efficacy Endpoints
L325: **Safety:** Time to first occurrence of adjudicated MACE (composite of all-cause mortality, nonfatal MI, and nonfatal stroke)
L326: **Efficacy:** Mean change in Hb between Baseline and EP (Weeks 24 to 52).
L327: ## Secondary Efficacy Endpoints
L328: - Hb change from Baseline to Week 52
- N (%) responders, defined as having a mean Hb within the Hb analysis range 10 to 11.5 g/dL during EP
- % time Hb in analysis range during the EP
- Time to stopping randomized treatment due to meeting rescue criteria
L329: ## Exploratory Endpoints
L330: - Number (%) of participants who receive at least one RBC or whole blood transfusions by Week 52 and by end of treatment
- Number of RBC and whole blood transfusions per 100 person years
L331: The key secondary safety endpoints tested for superiority and adjusted for multiplicity included:
L332: - Time to MACE4
- Time to first occurrence of MACE or a TEE
- Time to first occurrence of MACE or HHF
- Time to progression of CKD among subjects with baseline eGFR \ge 15 \text{ mL/min}/1.73\text{m}^2 defined as: (a) 40% decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from baseline (confirmed 4 to 13 weeks later), or (b) ESRD as defined by either initiating chronic dialysis for \ge 90 days or not initiating chronic dialysis when dialysis is indicated or kidney transplantation
L333: Conditional on both co-primary endpoints ruling out their risk margins, key secondary endpoints would be tested for superiority by comparing the one-sided superiority p-value against the rank-associated alpha derived from the Holm-Bonferroni method.
L334: 4 Tested for noninferiority as a coprimary endpoint and tested for superiority as a key principal secondary endpoint.
L335: Adjudicated secondary safety endpoints in both trials are listed below. These endpoints are time-to-event endpoints.
L336: - All-cause mortality
- CV mortality
- Fatal or nonfatal MI
- Fatal or nonfatal stroke
- Fatal or nonfatal HHF
- Fatal or nonfatal TEE
- Composite of MACE and HHF5
- Composite of CV mortality and nonfatal MI
- Composite of MACE, HHF, and TEE
L337: ## Study Design
L338: Study 200808/ASCEND-ND was a randomized, open-label (sponsor blind), active-controlled, parallel-group, multi-center, event-driven study in patients with anemia associated with Non-Dialysis (ND)- CKD.
L339: This study comprised four study periods: a 4-week screening period, a 4-week placebo run-in period, a treatment period, and a follow-up period. Prior ESA therapy, if present, continued during the screening and run-in periods.
L340: The Treatment Period consists of (see Figure 7):
L341: - SP, defined as the period from Day 1 to Week 28 (up to but excluding the Week 28 visit), during which study treatment was dose-titrated to achieve and maintain Hb in the target range.
- MP, defined as the period from the end of the SP (Week 28) to the end of treatment (variable per participant), to assess long term safety and efficacy.
- EP, defined as the period from Week 28 to Week 52, during which Hb efficacy was primarily assessed.
- Alternative EP: Because of the importance of patients not spending undue time with suboptimal Hb levels, a shorter EP, defined as the period from Week 28 to Week 36, was also assessed for Hb efficacy.
L342: 5 A recurrent event with data on multiple events for analysis
L343: Figure 7. Study 200808/ASCEND-ND Schematic
L344: Source: Sponsor CSR
Abbreviations: CSR, clinical study report; ESA, erythropoiesis-stimulating agents; EU, European Union; Hgb, hemoglobin; RoW, rest of the world; US, United States
L345: In ASCEND-ND, subjects were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either oral daprodustat or to darbepoetin alfa SC. Daprodustat was dosed daily, while the control darbepoetin alfa was dosed weekly, every 2 weeks, or every 4 weeks, depending on the subject's prior ESA use.
L346: An anemia rescue algorithm, which included a provision for the use of intravenous iron, an RBC transfusion, or both, was provided in the protocols (details are provided in Section 16.4). Additionally, the protocol required subjects to be iron replete throughout the study – and initiate iron therapy (investigator's choice) if ferritin was less than or equal to 100 ng/mL, transferrin saturation was less than or equal to 20%, or both.
L347: ## Study Population Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria
L348: ## Inclusion Criteria
L349: The study recruited male and female (non-pregnant, non-lactating) participants, \ge 18 years to \le 99 years of age with anemia associated with CKD not on dialysis (Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative [KDOQI] stages 3, 4, or 5 defined by eGFR using the CKD Epidemiology Collaboration [CKD-EPI] formula) and who were either not using ESAs or were current ESA users:
L350: - Group 1 (not using ESAs): No ESA use within the 6 weeks prior to screening and no ESA use between screening and randomization (Day 1).
- Group 2 (ESA users): Use of any approved ESA for the 6 weeks prior to screening and continuing between screening and randomization.
L351: ## Exclusion Criteria
L352: - On dialysis or clinical evidence of impending need to initiate dialysis within 90 days after study start (Day 1).
- Planned kidney transplant within 52 weeks
- Ferritin \le 100 ng/mL (\le 100 \mug/L) at screening
L353: - TSAT \le20% at screening (If TSAT was 18 to 20%, a retest using a new blood sample could be obtained within 7 days of the final laboratory report; the final retest value must be &gt;20% to confirm eligibility)
- History of bone marrow aplasia or pure red cell aplasia
- Anemia other than anemia of CKD.
- MI, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, or transient ischemic attack within 4 weeks prior to screening through to randomization (Day 1)
- Bazett's correction of QT interval (QTcB) &gt;500 msec, or QTcB &gt;530 msec in participants with bundle branch block at randomization (Day 1)
- Chronic Class IV heart failure
- Uncontrolled hypertension
- Prior (within 2 years) or current history of cancer (with the exception of localized squamous cell or basal cell carcinoma of the skin), or complex kidney cyst (e.g., Bosniak Category II F, III or IV) &gt;3 cm.; current unstable liver or biliary disease or known hepatic or biliary abnormalities; or gastrointestinal bleeding.
- Participants requiring treatment with a strong inhibitor of CYP2C8 or a strong inducer of CYP2C8 were excluded.
L354: ## 6.2.2.2. Statistical Analysis Plan
L355: ## Sample Size Determination
L356: The size of this event driven trial was based on the co-primary CV safety objective and determined by a fixed event target of 664 adjudicated first MACE. This provided approximately 90% power to establish non-inferiority assuming a true underlying 3% lower relative risk of MACE in favor of daprodustat compared to darbepoetin alfa (i.e., HR=0.97) and 82% power for the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 1.25 under the assumption that the true underlying risk of MACE was the same in both arms (i.e., HR=1.00).
L357: For 90% power to test the co-primary non-inferiority Hb hypothesis, with a two-sided 95% CI, pre-specified margin of -0.75 g/dL and a two-sample t-test, a total of 86 evaluable participants per treatment group was required. The planned study size far exceeded this requirement and provided more than 99% power for non-inferiority and a high level of precision to estimate the treatment effect (two-sided 95% CI half width of 0.105 g/dL, assuming 30% of participants would be non-evaluable for efficacy). The largest (most negative) difference between arms that would meet the statistical criterion for non-inferiority would be -0.645 g/dL. If the two-sided 95% CI is completely negative (i.e., lies fully within the range -0.75 to &lt;0 g/dL) non-inferiority would still be concluded.
L358: ## Interim Analysis
L359: There were no prospectively defined interim analyses planned to stop the study early for benefit. While the planned futility analysis described below had a small impact on reducing study-wise Type I error rate, there were no plans to adjust the alpha level used for the final analysis.
L360: The IDMC evaluated the co-primary MACE endpoint to assess for futility of achieving non-inferiority at study completion. Pre-specified guidelines governing the decision to continue or
L361: stop the study considered signals for harm, the predictive probability of achieving at least non-inferiority at trial end, and the risk of incorrectly stopping for futility.
L362: ## Missing Data Handling for Primary Efficacy Endpoint (Hb)
L363: For each missing value between Baseline to Week 52 (inclusive), 200 imputed values for Hb were generated using multiple imputation. The pooled average of these 200 imputed values were used in the summary tables and figures. For co-primary efficacy Hb analysis and the corresponding subgroup analyses using all available observed and imputed Hb values (on and off-treatment), Rubin's rules were used to combine results of the imputed datasets. The MAR assumption was considered appropriate as it is expected that off-treatment Hb values were similar to on-treatment Hb values, since patients would usually take commercially available Darbepoetin medication during such times in order to control their Hb. A tipping point analysis was also performed as a sensitivity analysis for the assumptions of missing data, that is, to mimic MNAR in which the missing observations depend on unobserved values.
L364: ## Efficacy Analysis for Primary Endpoint
L365: The primary efficacy evaluation was the effect of daprodustat relative to darbepoetin alfa on the change in Hb from Baseline to the average of all values in the EP, regardless of adherence to treatment including interruptions and discontinuation, the use of nonrandomized ESA medication for any reason including rescue therapy or the use of blood transfusions, and assuming participants did not die before the end of the EP.
L366: For each participant, Baseline Hb was the value obtained prior to taking randomized treatment (Day 1 value, or if this was missing, Baseline Hb was the value obtained at the latest non-missing pre-dose assessment on or before the randomization date), and Hb during the EP was determined by calculating the mean of all available and imputed Hb values between Weeks 28 to 52 inclusive regardless of adherence to randomized treatment. Multiple imputation was used to impute missing Hb data, and an ANCOVA model, adjusting for region, current ESA use, Baseline hemoglobin, and treatment, was used to obtain a point estimate, the two-sided 95% CI for the treatment difference (daprodustat-darbepoetin alfa), and an associated one-sided noninferiority test p-value. Non-inferiority was established if the lower limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the treatment difference was greater than the margin of -0.75 g/dL.
L367: ## Sensitivity Analyses
L368: - Post-randomization Hb (Observed Values Only Analysis): An analysis using available observed Hb values (on and off-treatment) only for post-randomization hemoglobin. Missing Hb data were not imputed.
- Evaluable Hb: An alternative "while on-treatment" estimand using only evaluable Hb data. Missing Hb data were not imputed.
- PP Hb: A PP population analysis based on the evaluable Hb analysis.
- Alternative EP (Week 28-36) Analyses:An alternative EP analysis from Week 28-36 using all available Hb values (on and off treatment). Missing post-Baseline Hb values were imputed.
- An alternative EP analysis from Week 28-36 using only evaluable Hb values. Missing Hb data were not imputed.
L369: - A tipping point analysis using all available Hb values (on and off-treatment) as a sensitivity for the co-primary estimand and using evaluable Hb values as supportive analysis
- COVID-19 supportive analysis: a plot by calendar date (in quarters) of adjusted treatment difference in mean change in Hb from Baseline using all available Hb values (on and off-treatment) at each time point, to assess the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.
L370: ## Analyses for Secondary Efficacy Endpoints
L371: - For the mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) analysis of change from baseline in Hb, the non-inferiority (NI) margin used in the co-primary analysis of Hb (-0.75 g/dL) will be used for reference in this comparison, thus generating support for non-inferiority if the lower bound of the two-sided 95% CI is above -0.75 g/dL.
- For the responder analysis, the number and % of responders by treatment group, difference in response rate (daprodustat – darbepoetin alfa) and two-sided 95% CI using Wald method were provided along with the one-sided Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) p-value for the treatment group comparison.
- The % time Hb is above, in and below the Hb analysis range (10 to 11.5 g/dL) during the MP and the EP were summarized using mean, standard deviation, minimum, P25, median, P75, and maximum by treatment group.
L372: ## Multiple Comparisons
L373: The multiplicity strategy used a combination of a gatekeeper approach on the co-primary endpoints, followed by a closed-test multiplicity procedure wrapped around the family of superiority hypotheses consisting of MACE and the key secondary endpoints. Figure 8 illustrates the structure of the statistical testing plan. First, the co-primary endpoints were evaluated for non-inferiority by comparing either the lower bound (Hb) or the upper bound (MACE) of each two-sided 95% CI to the corresponding non-inferiority margin. Conditional on both co-primary endpoints achieving non-inferiority (i.e., passing the gatekeeper), the family of MACE and the key secondary endpoints were formally tested for superiority using the Holm-Bonferroni procedure. The procedure was conducted based on a family-wise Type I error rate set at the one-sided 2.5% level.
L374: **Figure 8. Multiplicity Controlled Statistical Testing Plan for Study 200808/ASCEND-ND**
L375: Source: Sponsor CSR
Abbreviations: CI, confidence interval; CKD, chronic kidney disease; CSR, clinical study report; IV, intravenous; MACE, major adverse cardiovascular events; MI, myocardial infarction
L376: ## Subgroup Analysis
L377: Subgroup analyses, including age, sex, region, current ESA use, and race were performed. For both the Hb change from baseline to Weeks 28 to 52 and the Hb responder during EP, the region and current ESA use at randomization subgroups were conducted in a method similar to that described for the primary and secondary ITT analyses.
L378: ## 6.2.2.3. Results of Analyses
L379: ## Patient Disposition
L380: Participants were considered to have completed the study if they completed all visits through the End of Study visit irrespective of whether they discontinued randomized treatment. Participants were also considered to have completed the study if they died while on study. Of 3872 participants in the ITT population, 3743 (97%) participants completed the study through the End of Study visit or died while on study. A total of 64 (3%) participants in the daprodustat group and 65 (3%) participants in the darbepoetin alfa group discontinued randomized treatment and withdrew from the study (see Table 17). **There were no differences between the treatment groups in time to withdrawal from the study.**

L416: ## Primary Efficacy Sensitivity Analysis
L417: For the analysis of the co-primary efficacy endpoint, a multiple imputation approach was used to handle missing Hb values. Missing scheduled Hb data were imputed based on the MAR assumption. However, it is important to examine the sensitivity of inferences to departures from the MAR assumption for the monotone missing data. A tipping point analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis for the assumptions of missing data, that is, to mimic MNAR in which the missing observations depend on unobserved values. Results of the tipping point analysis suggest that the extent of missing data would unlikely impact the conclusions of the co-primary efficacy analysis.
L418: ## Efficacy Results—Secondary Endpoints
L419: A supportive analysis was performed for the primary ITT analysis of post-randomization mean change in Hb between Baseline and over the EP, repeating the analysis using a shorter EP (Week 28 to 36). For each study the lower bound of the 95% CI for the treatment difference was greater than the prospectively defined non-inferiority margin of -0.75 g/dL, thus supporting the overall conclusion of non-inferiority of daprodustat (see Table 21). Results were consistent with the conclusion from the primary analysis.

L473: ## 6.2.3. Study 204837/ASCEND-TD
L474: ## 6.2.3.1. Design
L475: ## Overview
L476: To support a three times a week dosing regimen in patients on hemodialysis, the Applicant conducted a randomized, Phase 3 Study, 204837/ASCEND-TD, titled “A Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, parallel-group, multi-center study in hemodialysis participants with anemia of chronic kidney disease to evaluate the efficacy, safety and pharmacokinetics of three-times weekly dosing of daprodustat compared to recombinant human erythropoietin, following a switch from recombinant human erythropoietin or its analogues.”
L477: ## Primary Efficacy Endpoint
L478: Mean change in Hb between Baseline and EP (Weeks 28 to 52)
L479: ## Key Secondary Efficacy Endpoint
L480: Average monthly IV iron dose (mg)/participant to Week 52
L481: ## Secondary Efficacy Endpoints
L482: - Hb change from Baseline to Week 52
- N (%) responders, defined as mean Hb within the Hb analysis range 10 to 11.5 g/dL during EP
- % time Hb in analysis range during the EP
- Time to stopping randomized treatment due to meeting rescue criteria
L483: ## Study Design
L484: Study 204837/ASCEND-TD was a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, double-dummy, parallel-group, multi-center study in hemodialysis-dependent participants, including combination methods such as hemodiafiltration or hemofiltration with hemodialysis, who had anemia of CKD and were being treated with rhEPO or its analogues.
L485: This study comprised a 4-week Screening Period, a 52-week Treatment Period and a Follow-up Period (Figure 12).
L486: The 52-week Treatment Period consists of:
L487: - SP, defined as the period from Day 1 to Week 28 (up to but excluding the Week 28 visit), during which study treatment was dose-titrated to achieve and maintain Hb in the target range.
- EP, defined as the period from Week 28 to Week 52, to assess long-term efficacy and safety. Throughout the trial, including during the EP, randomized treatment was titrated (in a double-blind fashion) according to a prespecified algorithm.
L488: Figure 12. Study Schematic for Study 204837/ASCEND-TD
L489: Source: Sponsor CSR
L490: Abbreviations: CSR, clinical study report; CV, coefficient of variation; HD, hemodialysis; Hgb, hemoglobin; PK/PD, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic; rhEPO, recombinant human erythropoietin
L491: Randomization was stratified by region and participants were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to either:
L492: - Daprodustat TIW + saline IV injection (placebo), or;
- Epoetin alfa once weekly or TIW (depending on dose level) + placebo tablets.
L493: ## Study Population Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria
L494: ## *Inclusion Criteria*
L495: The study recruited male and female (non-pregnant, non-lactating) participants, aged \ge18 years to \le99 years of age with anemia of CKD who were being treated with rhEPO or its analogues. Participants were hemodialysis-dependent (including hemofiltration or hemodiafiltration) for greater than 90 days and receiving hemodialysis (in-center) \ge3 times per week. Hb eligibility range is defined as:
L496: - Week -4: Hb 8 to 11.5 g/dL (5 to 7.4 mmol/L); If Hb is 11.6 to 11.9 g/dL (7.2 to 7.4 mmol/L), up to two retests are allowed; the retest value must be between 8 to 11.5 g/dL (5 to 7.1 mmol/L).
- Day 1: Hb 8 to 11 g/dL (5 to 6.8 mmol/L) and receiving at least the minimum rhEPO or analogue dose; Hb &gt;11 g/dL to 11.5 g/dL (6.8 to 7.1 mmol/L) and receiving greater than the minimum rhEPO or analogue dose
L497: ## *Exclusion Criteria*
L498: - Planned kidney transplant within 52 weeks
- Ferritin \le100 ng/mL (\le100 \mug/L) at screening
- TSAT \le20% at screening
L499: - History of bone marrow aplasia or pure red cell aplasia
- Anemia other than anemia of CKD.
- MI, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, or transient ischemic attack within 4 weeks prior to screening through to randomization (Day 1)
- QTcB &gt;500 msec, or QTcB &gt;530 msec in participants with bundle branch block at randomization (Day 1)
- Chronic Class IV heart failure
- Uncontrolled hypertension
- Prior or current history of cancer; liver disease or known hepatic or biliary abnormalities; or gastrointestinal bleeding.
- Participants requiring treatment with strong inhibitor of CYP2C8 or a strong inducer of CYP2C8 were excluded.
L500: ## 6.2.3.2. Statistical Analysis Plan
L501: ## Sample Size Determination
L502: Approximately 402 participants were planned to be randomized in a 2:1 ratio to daprodustat TIW or rhEPO (268 to the daprodustat TIW arm and 134 to the rhEPO arm), to provide at least 100 participants exposed to daprodustat for one year. Participants were treated to achieve and maintain Hb between 10 and 11 g/dL. The expected difference in mean Hb change from baseline and the EP, between arms, was 0 g/dL and the anticipated between participant standard deviation (SD) was 1.5 g/dL, based on historical rhEPO trials and daprodustat clinical trial experience to date. With a prespecified non-inferiority margin of -0.75 g/dL, a two-sample t-test and assuming that up to approximately 10% of participants had no Hb values measured during the EP, 402 randomized participants would provide &gt;90% power to test the primary hypothesis.
L503: With 402 randomized participants, it was anticipated that the difference in mean Hb change from baseline between arms would be estimated with a precision of 0.33 g/dL (half width of the two-sided 95% CI) and the largest (most negative) difference between arms that would meet the statistical criterion for non-inferiority would be -0.42 g/dL.
L504: ## Interim Analysis
L505: No interim analyses were performed.
L506: ## Missing Data
L507: For the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint, a multiple imputation approach was used to handle missing Hb values. Both intermittent missing and monotone missing scheduled Hb data were imputed based on the MAR assumption. However, it is important to examine the sensitivity of inferences to departures from the MAR assumption for the monotone missing data. A tipping point analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis for the assumptions of missing data, that is, to mimic MNAR in which the missing observations depend on unobserved values.
L508: ## Primary Efficacy Analysis
L509: The primary analysis of post-randomization mean change in Hb between baseline and over the EP (Weeks 28 to 52) for the ITT population was analyzed using an ANCOVA model adjusted for treatment, baseline Hb and region.
L510: ## Sensitivity Analyses
L511: - An alternative “while on-treatment” estimand using only evaluable Hb data. Missing Hb data were not imputed.
- PP population analysis based on the evaluable Hb analysis.
- A tipping point analysis using all available Hb values (on and off treatment) as a sensitivity analysis for the primary estimand. Missing post-baseline Hb values were imputed.
- A tipping point analysis using only evaluable Hb values. Missing Hb data were not imputed.
- An alternative EP analysis from Week 28 to 36 using all available Hb values (on and off treatment). Missing post-baseline Hb values were imputed.
- An alternative EP analysis from Week 28 to 36 using only evaluable Hb values. Missing Hb data were not imputed.
L512: ## Secondary Efficacy Analyses
L513: An ANCOVA model was used to compare the difference in average monthly IV iron dose per participant between arms, adjusting for treatment, baseline monthly IV iron dose and region.
L514: A least square mean estimates and two-sided 95% CI for the treatment difference are provided, together with the one-sided superiority test p-value.
L515: The secondary analysis of Hb change from baseline to Week 52 Hb was tested for noninferiority using the -0.75 g/dL margin used in the primary analysis. A MMRM approach was used with an unstructured covariance matrix to compare the difference in means between arms. The model was fitted to Hb data collected post-baseline up to Week 52, excluding values collected during the SP (Day 1 to Week 28). The model included factors for treatment, time, region, baseline Hb and the baseline Hb by time and treatment by time interaction terms.
L516: For the Hb responder analysis, responders were participants with a mean Hb during the EP that fell within the Hb analysis range of 10 to 11.5 g/dL. A CMH chi-squared test, adjusting for treatment and region, was used to compare the number and % of responders between the treatment groups.
L517: For the analysis of time to stopping study treatment due to meeting rescue criteria, a Cox proportional hazards model, adjusting for treatment and region, was used to generate the hazard ratio and associated 95% CI for the treatment group comparison. A one-sided superiority p-value was generated using a Wald test. The incidence rate per 100 person-years (PY) and associated 95% CI for each treatment group, as well as the absolute rate difference per 100 PY and associated 95% CI were also provided.
L518: ## Multiple Comparison
L519: The primary endpoint was tested first for non-inferiority, using the lower limit of the two-sided 95% CI. Conditional on achieving statistical significance (i.e., establishing non-inferiority) the single key secondary endpoint was tested for superiority using a one-sided 2.5% significance level. This two-step hierarchical strategy preserved the study-wise Type I error rate at a one-sided 2.5% level.
L520: The additional secondary/exploratory endpoints, if tested, were not adjusted for multiplicity. A nominal one-sided 2.5% significance level was applied per test.
L521: ## Subgroup Analysis
L522: Post hoc subgroup analyses, including age, sex, region, and race were performed for the primary ITT analysis of post-randomization mean change in Hb between baseline and over the EP (Weeks 28 to 52).
L523: ## 6.2.3.3. Results of Analyses
L524: ## Patient Disposition
L525: Participants were considered to have completed the study if they remained on study to Week 52 and completed the Week 52 visit irrespective of whether they discontinued randomized treatment. Participants were also considered to have completed the study if they died while on study. Of 407 participants in the ITT population, 404 (&gt;99%) participants completed the study to Week 52 or died while on study. One (&lt;1%) participant in the daprodustat TIW group and 2 (1%) participants in the epoetin alfa group discontinued randomized treatment and withdrew from the study (see Table 28).

L566: ## Sensitivity Analysis
L567: For the analysis of the Hb co-primary efficacy endpoint, a multiple imputation approach was used to handle missing Hb values. Missing scheduled Hb data were imputed based on the MAR assumption. However, it is important to examine the sensitivity of inferences to departures from the MAR assumption for the monotone missing data. A tipping point analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis for the assumptions of missing data, that is, to mimic MNAR in which the missing observations depend on unobserved values.
L568: Results of the tipping point analysis suggest that the extent of missing data would unlikely impact the conclusions of the primary/co-primary efficacy analysis. Therefore, missing data in these studies are unlikely to have had an impact on the primary results.

L625: ## 6.2.4. Study 201410/ASCEND-ID
L626: ## 6.2.4.1. Design
L627: ## Overview
L628: (b) (4) Applicant conducted a randomized, Phase 3 Study, 201410/ASCEND-ID, titled “A 52-week open-label (sponsor-blind), randomized, active-controlled, parallel-group, multi-center study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of daprodustat compared to recombinant human erythropoietin in subjects with anemia associated with chronic kidney disease who are initiating dialysis.”
L629: ## Primary Efficacy Endpoint
L630: Mean change in Hb between Baseline and EP (Weeks 28 to 52)
L631: ## Key Secondary Efficacy Endpoint
L632: Average monthly IV iron dose (mg)/participant to Week 52
L633: ## Secondary Efficacy Endpoints
L634: - Hb change from Baseline to Week 52
- N (%) responders, defined as mean Hb within the Hb analysis range 10 to 11.5 g/dL during EP
- % time Hb in analysis range during the EP
- Time to stopping randomized treatment due to meeting rescue criteria
L635: ## Study Design
L636: Study 201410/ASCEND-ID was a Phase 3, randomized, open-label (sponsor blind), active-controlled, parallel-group, multi-center study in participants with anemia associated with CKD who were initiating dialysis. The study comprised 3 periods: a screening period of 2 weeks (which could be extended by an additional 4 weeks for kidney ultrasound examination, IV iron supplementation and/or vitamin B12 treatment as needed), a 52-week active treatment period, and a follow-up period of 4 to 6 weeks (Figure 16).
L637: Participants were stratified by dialysis type to either hemodialysis, or peritoneal dialysis and by whether their dialysis start was planned or unplanned (urgent). Following stratification, participants were randomized 1:1 to receive daprodustat or darbepoetin alfa. During the treatment period, iron therapy was supplied and administered locally.
L638: The treatment period consisted of:
L639: - The SP, defined as the period from Day 1 to Week 28 during which randomized treatment was dose titrated to achieve the appropriate Hb target of 10.0 to 11.0 g/dL.
- The EP, defined as the period from the end of the stabilization period (Week 28) to Week 52, to assess safety and efficacy. If required, randomized treatment could be dose titrated to achieve or maintain Hb level in the target range.
L640: Figure 16. Study Schematic 201410/ASCEND-ID
L641: * Screening period may be extended by an additional 4 weeks for ultrasound examination, IV iron supplementation and/or vitamin B12 treatment as needed.
L642: Source: Sponsor CSR
Abbreviations: CSR, clinical study report; F/up, follow-up; IV, intravenous
L643: ## Study Population Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria
L644: ## *Key Inclusion Criteria*
L645: - Age (confirmed at screening): 18 to 99 years of age inclusive, male and female (non-pregnant, non-lactating) participants.
- Dialysis: participants were planning to start chronic dialysis within the next 6 weeks (from the date of the screening visit) OR had started and received dialysis (as specified below) for end-stage renal disease for a maximum of ≤90 days immediately prior to randomization and were not expected to stop dialysis during the duration of the trial:
L646: - hemodialysis: \ge 2 times/week.
- Peritoneal Dialysis: \ge 4 times/week including incremental schedule; participants on continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis and automated peritoneal dialysis were eligible.
- Hb concentration as measured by HemoCue (range inclusive): 8.0 to 10.5 g/dL (5.0 to 6.5 mmol/L) at screening and 8.0 to 11.0 g/dL (5.0 to 6.8 mmol/L) at randomization.
L647: ## *Key Exclusion Criteria*
L648: - Planned living-related or living-unrelated kidney transplant during the study.
- Ferritin \le 100 ng/mL (\le 100 \mug/L) at screening or after IV iron supplementation.
- TSAT \le 20\% at screening or after IV iron supplementation.
- History of bone marrow aplasia or pure red cell aplasia.
- Other causes of anemia.
- Use of any ESA treatment within 8 weeks prior to screening except for limited use as part of dialysis initiation (see the Protocol, Section 5.2 for details).
- MI, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, or transient ischemic attack: \le 10 weeks prior to screening through to randomization (Day 1).
- Heart failure.
- Current uncontrolled hypertension.
- QTcB (Day 1): QTcB &gt;500 msec, or QTcB &gt;530 msec in participants with bundle branch block.
- Previous or current history of malignancy; unstable liver disease; or gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding.
- Use of strong cytochrome P450 CYP2C8 inhibitors or strong CYP2C8 inducers.
- Any prior treatment with daprodustat for &gt;30 days.
L649: ## 6.2.4.2. Statistical Analysis Plan
L650: ## Sample Size Determination
L651: The size of this study was determined based on the following criteria: (1) to be sufficient to meet the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) E1 guideline for participant exposure, number, and duration; and (2) to provide at least 90% power to test the primary non-inferiority hypothesis with a 2-sided 95% CI.
L652: With a pre-specified non-inferiority margin of -0.75 g/dL and a 2-sided 95% CI, approximately 300 randomized participants (150 per treatment group) were deemed sufficient to provide &gt;90% power to test the primary hypothesis and to provide safety data on at least 100 participants exposed to daprodustat for 1 year.
L653: ## Interim Analysis
L654: The IDMC periodically received unblinded safety reports containing, at a minimum, clinical endpoints (whether adjudicated or pending adjudication) and serious adverse events (SAEs) from an independent statistical data analysis center while the study was ongoing. There were no prospectively defined interim analyses planned to stop the study early for Hb efficacy or futility.
L655: ## Missing Data
L656: For the analysis of the co-primary efficacy endpoint, a multiple imputation approach was used to handle missing Hb values. Both intermittent missing and monotone missing scheduled Hb data were imputed based on the MAR assumption. However, it is important to examine the sensitivity of inferences to departures from the MAR assumption for the monotone missing data. A tipping point analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis for the assumptions of missing data, that is, to mimic MNAR in which the missing observations depend on unobserved values.
L657: ## Primary Efficacy Analysis
L658: The primary Hb efficacy analysis assessed the estimand defined as the comparative treatment effect in mean Hb change between Baseline and EP (i.e., Weeks 28 to 52 inclusive) in all randomized participants i.e., the ITT population. An ANCOVA model adjusted for randomization stratification factors (dialysis type and dialysis start manner), Baseline Hb, and treatment was used. All Hb data (on- and off-treatment) recorded during the EP was included in the primary efficacy analysis, regardless of adherence to randomized treatment including interruptions and discontinuations, the use of non-randomized ESA medication for any reason including rescue therapy, or the use of blood transfusions. Multiple imputation was applied in the case of missing Hb data.
L659: Participants were analyzed according to the treatment to which they were randomized using an ANCOVA model. The analysis tested whether daprodustat was non-inferior to darbepoetin alfa. The non-inferiority margin was pre-defined as -0.75 \text{ g/dL}, determined based upon a combination of clinical judgment, statistical reasoning, and regulatory guidance for designing non-inferiority trials. Non-inferiority would be established if the lower limit of the 2-sided 95% CI for the treatment difference in mean Hb change between Baseline and EP (daprodustat - darbepoetin alfa) was greater than 0.75 \text{ g/dL}.
L660: ## Sensitivity Analyses
L661: - An alternative “while on-treatment” estimand using only evaluable Hb data. Missing Hb data were not imputed.
- PP population analysis based on the on-treatment evaluable Hb analysis.
- A tipping point analysis using all available Hb values (on- and off-treatment) as a sensitivity analysis for the primary estimand. Missing post-baseline Hb values were imputed.
- A tipping point analysis similar to the one described above was performed as a sensitivity analysis for this estimand using evaluable Hb values only.
- An alternative EP analysis from Weeks 28 to 36 using all available Hb values (on and off treatment). Missing post-baseline Hb values were imputed.
- An alternative EP analysis from Weeks 28 to 36 using only evaluable Hb values. Missing Hb data were not imputed.
- A post-hoc analysis, which included all available observed post-randomization hemoglobin values (on and off-treatment), evaluated the mean change in hemoglobin between Baseline to the evaluation period (Week 28 to 52).
L662: ## Secondary Efficacy Analyses
L663: The planned key secondary efficacy analysis was the on-treatment average monthly IV iron dose (mg)/participant from Baseline to Week 52 excluding IV iron use following a participant's first RBC or whole blood transfusion and was based on the ITT population. An ANCOVA model was used to compare the difference in average monthly IV iron dose per participant between treatment groups, adjusting for: treatment; Baseline monthly IV iron dose; dialysis type; and dialysis start manner. The number and percentage of participants with Baseline IV iron use, on treatment EP IV iron use, and on-treatment IV iron use to Week 52 was summarized by treatment.
L664: The secondary analysis of Hb change from baseline to Week 52 Hb was tested for non-inferiority using the -0.75 g/dL margin used in the primary analysis. A MMRM approach was used with an unstructured covariance matrix to compare the difference in means between groups. The model included factors for treatment, time, prognostic randomization factors (dialysis type and dialysis start manner), Baseline Hb, and the Baseline Hb by time and treatment by time interaction terms. This analysis was performed using all available Hb values (on- and off-treatment) and separately using evaluable Hb values only.
L665: For the analysis of % time Hb in range (10.0 to 11.5 g/dL) during the EP (Weeks 28 to 52), the method by Rosendaal was used to calculate the percentage of time (days) a participant's Hb was below, within and above the Hb analysis range during the EP. Non-inferiority with the margin of -0.75 g/dL was assessed using the Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the median treatment difference and associated 95% CI, comparing the percentage of time in range between treatment groups. Superiority was assessed using the 1-sided p-value from a van Elteren test (stratified Wilcoxon rank sum test). The stratified Mann-Whitney estimator stratified by dialysis type and dialysis start manner, and 95% CI for the probability of daprodustat achieving a greater percentage of time with Hb in the analysis range than darbepoetin alfa provided a supportive treatment comparison estimate for the van Elteren test.
L666: For the Hb responder analysis, responders were participants with a mean Hb during the EP that fell within the Hb analysis range of 10.0 to 11.5 g/dL. A Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel chi-squared test, adjusting for treatment, dialysis type, and dialysis start manner, was used to compare the number and % of responders between the treatment groups.
L667: For the analysis of time to stopping randomized treatment due to meeting rescue criteria, a Cox proportional hazards model, adjusting for treatment, dialysis start type, and dialysis start manner (planned or unplanned) was used to generate the hazard ratio and associated 95% CI for the treatment group comparison. A 1-sided superiority p-value was generated using a Wald test. The incidence rate per 100 PY and associated 95% CI for each treatment group, as well as the absolute rate difference per 100 PY and associated 95% CI were also provided.
L668: ## Multiple Comparison
L669: The primary endpoint was tested first for non-inferiority, using the lower limit of the 2-sided 95% CI. Conditional on achieving statistical significance (i.e., passing the primary gate by establishing non-inferiority) the single key secondary endpoint was tested for superiority using a 1-sided 2.5% significance level. This 2-step hierarchical strategy was implemented to preserve the study-wise Type I error rate at a 1-sided 2.5% significance level.
L670: The additional secondary/exploratory endpoints were not to be adjusted for multiplicity – a nominal 1-sided 2.5% significance level was applied per test.
L671: ## Subgroup Analysis
L672: Subgroup analyses, including age, sex, and race were performed for the primary ITT analysis of post-randomization mean change in Hb between Baseline and over the EP (Weeks 28 to 52). Subgroup analysis were performed using all available observed and imputed Hb values (on and off-treatment). Rubin's rules were used to combine results of the imputed datasets.
L673: ## 6.2.4.3. Results of Analyses

Participants were also considered to have completed the study if they died while on study. L708: ## Sensitivity Analysis
L709: For the analysis of the Hb co-primary efficacy endpoint in the active controlled studies, a multiple imputation approach was used to handle missing Hb values. Missing scheduled Hb data were imputed based on the MAR assumption. However, it is important to examine the sensitivity of inferences to departures from the MAR assumption for the monotone missing data. A tipping point analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis for the assumptions of missing data, that is, to mimic MNAR in which the missing observations depend on unobserved values.
L710: Results of the tipping point analysis suggest that the extent of missing data would unlikely impact the conclusions of the Hb co-primary efficacy analysis. Therefore, missing data in these studies are unlikely to have had an impact on the primary results.

L765: ## 6.2.5. Study 205270/ASCEND NHQ
L766: ## 6.2.5.1. Design
L767: ## Overview
L768: The Applicant conducted a randomized, Phase 3 Study, 205270/ASCEND NHQ, titled “A 28-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multi-center, study in recombinant human erythropoietin (rhEPO) naïve non-dialysis participants with anemia associated with chronic kidney disease to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and effects on quality of life of daprodustat compared to placebo.”
L769: ## Primary Efficacy Endpoint
L770: Mean change in Hb between Baseline and EP (Weeks 24 to 28)
L771: ## Key Secondary Efficacy Endpoints
L772: % of participants having a Hb increase of \ge 1.0 g/dL from Baseline to EP (Weeks 24 to 28)
Mean change in SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain between Baseline and Week 28
L773: ## Secondary Efficacy Endpoints
L774: - Hb change from Baseline to Week 28
- N (%) responders, defined as mean Hb within the Hb analysis range 11 to 12 g/dL during EP
- % time Hb in analysis range during the EP
- Time to stopping randomized treatment due to meeting rescue criteria
L775: - Mean change from baseline by domain and overall symptom score on the Chronic Kidney Disease-Anemia (CKD-AQ) symptom questionnaire
- Change from baseline in the Patient Global Impression of Severity (PGI-S)
L776: ## Study Design
L777: This was a 28-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multi-center Phase 3 study in participants with anemia associated with CKD who were not on dialysis. This study enrolled participants who had a Hb of 8.5 to 10.0 g/dL, inclusive, as measured by a point-of-care Hb analyzer (HemoCue). These participants had limited history of IV iron administration and were rHPO naïve prior to Screening and Randomization.
L778: The study included a 4-week Screening period, a 28-week Treatment period, and a 4-week Follow-up period (Figure 20). The total duration of study participation for each participant was approximately 36 weeks. Rescreening was allowed up to 2 additional times.
L779: **Figure 20. Study Schematic (Study 205270/ASCEND-NHQ)**
L780: Source: Sponsor's CSR
Abbreviations: CSR, clinical study report; Hgb, hemoglobin
L781: Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive either daprodustat or matching placebo tablets. Daprodustat and placebo doses for participants were titrated based upon HemoCue Hb. Dose modifications for these participants followed a protocol-specified dose adjustment algorithm to achieve and maintain Hb within the target range of 11.0 to 12.0 g/dL, inclusive. Dose changes were made programmatically in a blinded fashion by the IRT system in order to ensure that investigators and participants stayed blinded to the study treatment and the dose adjustments.
L782: A rescue algorithm was provided to minimize participants having an inadequate response to the treatment for their anemia for an extended period of time and to enable rescue therapy to be provided to the participants based on local clinical practice (Section 16.4).
L783: A Clinical Events Committee adjudicated any event suspected to be MACE.
L784: ## Study Population
L785: Participants were eligible for inclusion in this study only if all of the protocol-specified criteria applied at Screening (Week -4 and Week -2) and Randomization (Day 1), unless otherwise specified. Key inclusion and exclusion criteria are summarized below.
L786: ## Key Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria
L787: ## Inclusion Criteria
L788: - Male or female participants \ge 18 years of age, at the time of signing the informed consent.
- CKD confirmed at Screening: Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (KDOQI) CKD stages 3, 4, or 5 defined by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) using the CKD Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI) formula.
- Stable HemoCue Hb from 8.5 to 10.5, inclusive, at the Screening visit (Week -4) and from 8.5 to 10.0 g/dL, inclusive, at Randomization (Day 1).
- Treatment with up to one IV iron dose within the 8 weeks prior to Screening and no IV iron use between the Screening visit and Randomization (Day 1). If needed, stable oral iron supplementation was permitted (&lt;50% change in overall dose maintenance and no change in type of iron prescribed doses in the 4 weeks prior to Day 1 Randomization visit).
L789: ## Exclusion Criteria
L790: - Dialysis or clinical evidence of impending need to initiate dialysis within 180 days after Randomization (Day 1).
- Planned living-related or living-unrelated kidney transplant within 28 weeks after Randomization (Day 1).
- Low values of ferritin or transferrin saturation (TSAT) at Screening.
- History of rhEPO or rhEPO analogue use within the 8 weeks prior to Screening and rhEPO use between Screening and Randomization (Day 1).
- History of transfusion within the 8 weeks prior to Screening and transfusion between Screening and Randomization (Day 1).
- History of bone marrow aplasia or pure red cell aplasia.
- Megaloblastic anemia (untreated pernicious anemia and folate deficiency), thalassemia major, sickle cell disease, or myelodysplastic syndrome.
- Evidence of actively bleeding gastric, duodenal, or esophageal ulcer disease or clinically significant GI bleeding \le 8 weeks prior to Screening through Randomization (Day 1).
- QTcB &gt;500 msec or QTcB &gt;530 msec in participants with Bundle Branch Block. There was no QTc exclusion for participants with a predominantly paced rhythm.
- For participants residing in Italy, QTcB exclusion criteria were replaced with QTcF criteria: QTcF &gt;470 ms (females) and &gt;450 ms (males) pre-dose prior to Randomization (Day 1) and presence of second or third degree AV block.
- Malignancy within 2 years of Screening through Randomization (Day 1), currently receiving treatment for cancer, or had a known complex kidney cyst &gt;3 cm.
- Any prior treatment with daprodustat for &gt;30 days.
- Ferric citrate use within 4 weeks prior to Randomization (Day 1).
- Significant CV or hepatic disease.
L791: ## 6.2.5.2. Statistical Analysis Plan
L792: Approximately 600 participants were planned to be randomized (300 per arm) to receive daprodustat or placebo, who would be treated to achieve and maintain Hb between 11 and
L793: 12 g/dL. The primary efficacy endpoint was the mean change in Hb between baseline and over the EP (mean of all available [on and off treatment] Hb values for Week 24 through Week 28, inclusive, including any unscheduled Hb values that were taken during this time period). For the primary endpoint, the expected difference in mean Hb change from baseline and the EP, between arms, was 1.0 g/dL and the anticipated between participant standard deviation was 1.5 g/dL, based on historical rhEPO trials and daprodustat clinical trial experience to date. For additional details on the statistical analysis plan refer to Section 16.1.3.
L794: ## 6.2.5.3. Results of Analyses
L795: ## Patient Disposition
L796: Participants were considered to have completed the study if they completed the 28 Week treatment period and the follow-up visit irrespective of whether they discontinued randomized treatment. Participants were also considered to have completed the study if they died while on study. Of 614 participants in the ITT population, 590 (96%) participants completed the study to Week 28 or died while on study. Seven participants (2%) in the daprodustat group and 17 participants (6%) in the placebo group discontinued randomized treatment and withdrew from the study (Table 52).

L825: ## Efficacy Results—Primary Endpoint
L826: Mean Baseline Hb was similar between the treatment groups (See Figure 21). L882: ## 6.3. Key Efficacy Review Issues
L883: ## 6.3.1. Use of Rescue Therapy in the ASCEND Program
L884: ## Issue
L885: Impact of Rescue Therapy Use on the Non-Inferiority Efficacy Conclusion of Daprodustat
L886: ## Background
L887: Hb response and reduction in transfusion need have been accepted endpoints for establishing clinical benefit in patients with anemia of CKD. The ASCEND-D and ASCEND-ND trials used Hb response at the primary efficacy period of 28-52 weeks as the primary efficacy endpoint. The pre-specified non-inferiority Hb comparisons used -0.75 g/dL as the non-inferiority margin, which was appropriately justified based on previous applications for drugs intended to treat anemia of CKD and statistical reasoning. An evaluation of the time to stopping randomized treatment due to meeting rescue criteria was evaluated as a secondary efficacy endpoint in the ASCEND-D and ASCEND-ND study to further evaluate the robustness of the efficacy results.
L888: ## Assessment
L889: ## ASCEND-D
L890: The cumulative incidence for time to stopping randomized treatment due to meeting rescue criteria was similar between the treatment groups (Table 61).

L909: ## ASCEND-ND
L910: The proportion of participants stopping randomized treatment due to meeting rescue criteria was 2% in the daprodustat arm compared to 3% participants in the darbepoetin alfa arm. One subject met the rescue criteria but did not discontinue randomized treatment (Table 63).

L928: ## Conclusion
L929: The above results support the non-inferiority conclusion of the efficacy of daprodustat on Hb. We expect the similarity in Hb response between daprodustat and the ESA control arms to translate into similar reductions in the need for RBC transfusions, an accepted clinical benefit for treatments for anemia of CKD, because of avoiding the procedure and its attendant risks.
L930: ## 6.3.2. Lack of Clinical Meaningfulness on Key Secondary Endpoint of SF-26 V2.0 Vitality Domain Score in ASCEND-NHQ
L931: ## Issue
L932: Lack of Clinical Meaningfulness on Key Secondary Endpoint of SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain score in ASCEND-NHQ.
L933: - Sub-Issue 1: The Applicant's proposed 6-point improvement threshold in the 0-100 scaled SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain score did not represent a clinically meaningful within-patient improvement.
- Sub-Issue 2: A meaningful treatment effect was not demonstrated upon review of the data from the secondary PRO endpoint of change from baseline to Week 28 in the 0-100 scaled SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain score.
L934: ## Background
L935: ## Sub-Issue 1
L936: The Applicant proposed a 6-point reduction (improvement) in the 0-100 scaled SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain score as a clinically meaningful within-patient change based on literature review and distribution-based and anchor-based methodologies. During the IND phase (IND 101291), we had advice regarding the Applicant's approach to deriving the threshold(s) for meaningful within-patient score change for the SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain (i.e., identified several limitations with using a literature review to derive threshold(s) for meaningful within-patient score change, recommended using an anchor-based analysis supplemented with both empirical cumulative distribution function [eCDF] and probability density function [PDF] curves). Ultimately, we concluded at that time that there was insufficient evidence to support that a 6-point improvement in the SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain score is a meaningful within-patient change. For additional details, refer to the Final Written Response dated December 4, 2019.
L937: ## Sub-Issue 2
L938: Although statistically significant results were reported on the key secondary endpoint of change from baseline to Week 28 in the 0-100 scaled SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain score, the difference between the daprodustat and placebo means was small. Minimal magnitude of changes was observed at the item- and domain-level of the SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain-score, using both raw and transformed score scales.
L939: ## Assessment
L940: ## Sub-Issue 1
L941: As part of the NDA, the Applicant submitted the “Patient-Reported Outcome Evidence Dossier for SF-36 Vitality domain and CKD-AQ in anemia due to Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)” Version 4.0 dated August 31, 2021 (hereafter referred to as the SF-36 PRO Dossier), which included findings from the literature review and anchor-based analyses.
L942: ## Literature Review
L943: FDA reviewed the Applicant's summary report of literature review (Appendix 16 of the SF-36 PRO Dossier) and noted much of the cited literature is based on approaches that are not aligned with FDA guidance (e.g., use of distribution-based methods, between-group differences). Based on FDA Guidance for Industry Patient-Reported Outcome Measures: Use in Medical Product Development to Support Labeling Claims, sponsors should use anchor-based methods6 to directly incorporate patients' perspective to help interpret the clinical meaningfulness of PRO endpoints. Other approaches, such as distribution-based approaches using an effect size or a standard deviation, or model-based approaches, are inappropriate as a primary method to determine clinical meaningfulness as they do not directly take into account the patient perspective. FDA concluded that the Applicant's literature review is not adequate
L944: ## Anchor-Based Analyses
L945: In response to the FDA's recommendation in the IND phase, the Applicant conducted anchor-based analyses using data from Studies ASCEND-ND and ASCEND-ID and derived a meaningful within-patient change threshold range of 6- to 21-point improvement (see Figure 25) based on 4 patient-reported anchor scales: PGI-S scale, Patient Global Impression of Change (PGI-C) scale, and items 1 and 2 from the CKD-AQ. The Applicant used the PGI-S and the PGI-C scales as the primary anchors and CKD-AQ items 1 and 2 as supportive anchors in the quantitative anchor-based analyses. Refer to Table 227 in Section 16.1 for a summary of the anchor scales.
L946: ## Figure 25. Excerpt of Text From Applicant's SF-36 PRO Dossier
L947: - +6 points: this threshold is based on changes observed in participants who had improved by +1 point on the PGI-S between Day 1 and Week 28 and changes observed among participants who reported being "very much improved" on the PGI-C at Week 28. +1 point improvements on the CKD-AQ Item 1 and 2 were 7.7 and 4.7 respectively and a moderate improvement on the PGI-C was 4.5. This threshold is also supported by consideration of mean and median definitions of meaningful change as reported in the research literature (Appendix 16).

L951: FDA identified limitations in the PGI-S and PGI-C anchor scales that limit the interpretability of the results of the anchor-based analyses. Specifically, the concepts measured in the SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain (tiredness, weakness, full of life, energy) were not aligned with the concepts measured in the PGI-S and PGI-C anchor scales (overall CKD symptoms). Due to these limitations, FDA focused on the Applicant's anchor-based analyses using items 1 and 2 from the CKD-AQ, which measure tiredness and energy that are better aligned with the SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain. As such, FDA considered the range of 18- to 21-point improvement appropriate based on the Applicant's anchor-based analyses results. Refer to the full COA review by the Division of Clinical Outcome Assessment (DCOA) for additional details on the adequacy of the anchor scales.
L952: Of note, while PRO data (e.g., SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain, CKD-AQ items 1 and 2) were collected in Studies ASCEND-ND and ASCEND-ID, the open-label study design of these two studies was a limitation to the interpretation of PRO data and subsequently the evaluation of clinically meaningful-within patient change, as it is unknown whether patients' knowledge of treatment assignment may lead to systematic overestimation or underestimation of the treatment effect, the magnitude of which is currently unknown. Therefore, FDA requested additional anchor-based analyses using Study ASCEND-NHQ data, which suggested a threshold range of 12.5- to 18.75-point improvement in the SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain score as clinically meaningful to patients. Of note, the Hb target in ASCEND-NHQ was higher than the other studies (11 to 12 g/dL, in contrast to 10 to 11 g/dL, which reflects current labeling for ESAs). The relevance of any efficacy conclusions to a population treated to a lower target is unclear.
L953: Refer to Section 16.1 of this review for more discussion on the anchor-based analyses.
L954: ## Sub-Issue 2

L971: ## Conclusion
L972: The Applicant's proposed 6-point improvement threshold in the 0-100 scaled SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain score did not represent a clinically meaningful within-patient improvement. Statistically significant results were reported on the key secondary endpoint of change from baseline to Week 28 in the 0-100 scaled SF-36 v2.0 Vitality domain-score in ASCEND-NHQ. However, FDA determined that these results did not substantiate a clinically meaningful improvement of daprodustat compared to placebo due to the minimal magnitude of changes observed at the item- and domain-level (using raw and transformed score scales), and modest to small between arm differences in response rates. In addition, the Hb target of 11 to 12 g/dL studied in ASCEND-NHQ is higher than the Hb target used in ASCEND-ND and ASCEND-D (i.e., higher than the target Hb used to establish the efficacy and safety of daprodustat for the approved use), further calling into question the relevance of the findings in ASCEND-NHQ.
L973: ## 6.1. Efficacy Summary
L974: After conducting a thorough evaluation of the ASCEND program, we agree with the Applicant that non-inferiority to an ESA comparator, based on hemoglobin response, was demonstrated in the DD, incident dialysis (ID), and NDD populations, and the DD population using three times a week dosing. We agree superiority was achieved against placebo for Hb in ASCEND-NHQ, but we do not agree a clinically important benefit was demonstrated on patient reported outcomes (See Section 6.3.2).
L975: Our non-inferiority conclusion was based on the prospectively defined and agreed upon primary endpoint, statistical test, and NI margin. The primary endpoint, change in Hb value between baseline and mean of values during Weeks 28 to 52, represents the key measurement used to clinically define anemia, averaged over a time frame sufficient to capture steady state. In constructing the NI margin of -0.75 g/dL, we considered Hb changes that would result in a clinically meaningful difference to an individual patient, proportion of comparator (i.e., ESAs) efficacy preserved by the margin, measurement variability, and precedent from prior trials (i.e., darbepoetin, peginesatide, and methoxy polyethylene glycol-epoetin beta). Non-inferiority was defined as being achieved if the two-sided lower 95% confidence limit for the mean treatment difference (daprodustat minus comparator) was greater than the pre-specified NI margin, as is customary. Although some ASCEND studies were open label, bias due to knowledge of treatment assignment was minimized by evidence of appropriate titration in the two treatment arms and the central laboratory-Hb objective endpoint.
L976: We found the conclusion of noninferiority to be robust to multiple sensitivity analyses which assessed the impact of important model assumptions, such as accounting for rescue therapy, endpoint missingness mechanisms (such as missing at random, or missing not at random), choice of analysis time window, and estimand strategy. We also generally found little heterogeneity between the subgroups studied, showing daprodustat was effective regardless of age, sex, race, body weight, dialysis type, CKD stage, prior ESA use, and Baseline Hb (Refer to Section 16).
L977: ## Regarding ASCEND-D and ASCEND-ND
L978: We placed particular emphasis on the efficacy results for ASCEND-D and ASCEND-ND, since it is well known hemoglobin can causally affect cardiovascular safety. In ASCEND-ND and ASCEND-D, the observed Hb versus time profile confirms that the titration algorithms resulted in similar Hb vs. time trajectories for daprodustat and the ESA comparator (Section 16). We are reassured that mean-level plots fell in the middle of the Hb target range for both arms during the EP. This provides assurance that the comparators were titrated and subsequently performed acceptably. In addition, the comparators performed reasonably similarly with other programs with regards to Hb vs. time. The within-subject variability in Hb data was also similar between arms. The proportion of participants who received transfusions during the evaluation period was generally similar between the daprodustat and ESA groups, as would be expected given the similarity of the achieved Hb levels (Section 6.3.1). Results from the key secondary analyses of the on-treatment monthly IV iron dose (mg/month) from Day 1 to Week 52 in ASCEND-D (not assessed in ASCEND-ND, due to infrequent indication for IV iron, but assessed in ASCEND-TD and ASCEND-ID) showed little or no difference between daprodustat and ESA in the mean IV iron dose. These supporting data further support the non-inferiority conclusion of the efficacy of daprodustat on Hb.
L979: Disposition and conduct during ASCEND-D and ASCEND-ND was not of concern. For each study, the treatment arms were balanced in relation to baseline demographics and clinical characteristics, with appropriate representation across ages, genders, and races/ethnicities. As mentioned above, we did not identify a heterogeneous efficacy response in a subgroup that warranted further study or concern. Importantly, follow-up was remarkably complete (&gt;95% of potential follow-up time was accounted for).
L980: In ASCEND-D and ASCEND-ND, the randomized treatment titration algorithm was prespecified. We reviewed the titration algorithms and determined they reflected reasonable
L981: clinical practice. Importantly, the target Hb range was 10 to 11 g/dL, which reflects current product labeling and best practice for ESA treatment. Instances where the algorithm was not explicitly followed were recorded as protocol violations. We reviewed the protocol violations, and they were balanced between arms. Additionally, rescue therapy and iron management criteria were prespecified and consistent across the ASCEND program.
L982: These conclusions were robust among all subgroups studied (including race, age, gender, location, prior ESA use, dialysis status), and to a standard battery of sensitivity analyses, which included alternative estimand strategies, evaluation periods, and data missingness assumptions. Several supportive analyses (both prespecified and post-hoc) for Hb such as Hb vs. time, time-in-range, and visit-to-visit variability were similarly balanced between arms. The incidence of RBC transfusions and rescue therapies was generally similar between treatment arms as well. These analyses further strengthen the conclusion of non-inferiority.
L983: ## Regarding ASCEND-ID, ASCEND-TD, and ASCEND-NHQ
L984: ASCEND-ID established non-inferiority of daprodustat for efficacy (mean change from baseline in Hb over evaluation period of Weeks 28 to 52) to darbepoetin in the ID population. As the study was not designed to demonstrate general safety or cardiovascular outcomes, (b) (4) it is unclear if the risks in this population (b) (4) will be similar to the NDD population or the DD population. Further discussion regarding cardiovascular safety in the ID population is in Section 6.2.4 and Section 7.7.6.
L985: In the ASCEND-TD, analysis of mean change in Hb between baseline over the evaluation period of Weeks 28 to 52 demonstrated that daprodustat TIW was non-inferior to epoetin alfa. The study was not designed to demonstrate general safety or cardiovascular outcomes. A detailed discussion of the CV safety and extrapolation of CV safety for the TIW dosing regimen in the DD population is in Section 7.7.5.
L986: ASCEND-NHQ established superiority for the primary efficacy endpoint of mean change in Hb between baseline over the evaluation period of Weeks 24 to 28 compared to placebo. It is important to note that the evaluation period in this trial was shorter than the other trials and the comparator arm was placebo. In addition, the target hemoglobin level was higher (11 to 12 g/dL) compared to 10 to 11 g/dL for all other trials in the ASCEND program. The principal secondary endpoint was a patient reported outcome (PRO), the mean change in SF-26 Vitality Domain between baseline and Week 28. We did not agree with the Applicant's conclusions regarding demonstrated benefit on the PRO. This is a key efficacy review issue discussed under Section 6.3.2.
L987: Lastly, for each ASCEND study, we reviewed the protocols, the statistical analysis plan, study report, and study data (Study Data Tabulation Model and Analysis Dataset Model). The quality of the original data submission was adequate. In general, the reviewers independently corroborated the Applicant's analyses using the submitted datasets.
L988: In conclusion, daprodustat increased Hb to a similar extent as approved ESAs (darbepoetin alfa in the NDD population and darbepoetin alfa or epoetin alfa in the DD population) with similar continued need for rescue therapy. Most patients with CKD receiving hemodialysis require ESAs to correct anemia and reduce the need for RBC transfusion and its attendant risks, including the risks of alloreactivity and rejection after kidney transplantation. We expect the similarity in Hb
L989: response and similarity in the need for rescue therapy between daprodustat and the ESA control arms to translate into similar reductions in the need for RBC transfusions, an accepted clinical benefit for treatments for anemia of CKD, because of avoiding the procedure and its attendant risks. There were no other benefits demonstrated on how patients feel, function, or survive.
L990: ## 7. Safety (Risk and Risk Management)
L991: ## 7.1. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Based on Nonclinical Data
L992: The safety of daprodustat and major human metabolites was evaluated in a comprehensive nonclinical program. Toxicological characterization was performed in good laboratory practice-compliant toxicology studies in mice, rats, dogs, and monkeys, in reproductive toxicology studies in rats and rabbits, and in a carcinogenicity assessment that included data from lifetime carcinogenicity studies in mice and rats. Monkeys were considered the most relevant nonclinical species for general toxicological evaluation based on the similarity of the daprodustat metabolite profile to humans and higher bioavailability compared to other species.
L993: Daprodustat binding was shown to be specific for HIF-prolyl hydroxylases in primary pharmacology and secondary pharmacology (evaluations of potential targets not associated with the desired therapeutic effect) assessments. No significant risks were identified during in vitro and in vivo cardiovascular, respiratory, or neurologic safety pharmacology assessments.
L994: Daprodustat is highly protein-bound in rats and rabbits (~100%), humans (&gt;99%), monkeys and dogs (~98%), and mice (&gt;99%). Because only the unbound fraction of drug is “active”, the high level of protein binding complicated the determination of appropriate exposure margins between nonclinical species and humans. Ultimately, exposure extrapolation based on body surface area (\text{mg}/\text{m}^2) was deemed the most appropriate method to inform clinical risk.
L995: The IND enabling nonclinical toxicology studies produced effects consistent with the exaggerated primary pharmacology of daprodustat (polycythemia) and secondary impacts on hemodynamics (systemic thrombosis, hemorrhage, congestion, and necrosis in lung, kidney, heart, and other organs). Thus, the clinical safety of daprodustat was predicted to be largely a function of its primary pharmacology and impacts on blood viscosity.
L996: In a 6-month toxicology study in non-anemic rats, adverse findings associated with excess hematocrit (e.g., thrombosis, hemorrhage, congestion, and necrosis occurred in various organs, along with splenomegaly, extramedullary hematopoiesis, and platelet reductions) at the highest dose of 10 \text{mg}/\text{kg}/\text{day} (4 times the clinical dose based on body surface area) in both sexes. In males, these effects caused mortality and moribundity leading to early termination of all high-dose male animals, which occurred coincident with total blood hematocrit levels as high as 75% at Week 13 (versus total blood hematocrit levels of 52% in untreated controls), whereas females tolerated similar effects on hematocrit. Daprodustat-related gastric hemorrhage, erosions and/or ulcerations also occurred due to downstream complications related to increased blood viscosity at the highest dose. In the 6-month rat study, the no-observed-adverse-effect-level (NOAEL) was determined to be 4 \text{mg}/\text{kg}/\text{day} (1.6 times the clinical dose based on body surface area), based on the mortality and daprodustat-related toxicity related to excess red blood cell mass observed at
L997: the highest dose of 10 mg/kg/day (4 times the clinical dose based on body surface area). The severity of findings increased with longer exposures, suggesting a potential for any negative impacts related to daprodustat to worsen over time. The narrow margin (2.5-fold dose-range) between the NOAEL and a severely toxic dose highlight a steep dose response curve for toxicity.
L998: The toxicologic profile observed in studies in non-anemic monkeys up to 9-months in duration was similar to that observed in long-term rat studies, with systemic thrombosis/hemorrhage linked to excess hematocrit (total hematocrits as high as 74% at the highest dose compared to 42% in controls) and platelet reductions observed at \ge 10 mg/kg/day (\ge 8 times the clinical dose based on body surface area). Findings also included dose-related gastric hemorrhage, erosions and/or ulcerations at \ge 10 mg/kg/day. At 50 mg/kg/day (40 times the clinical dose based on body surface area), widespread and severe impacts of polycythemia occurred, which included subacute inflammation, edema, and hemorrhage in the superficial brainstem and other evidence of systemic congestion and bleeding, underscoring the importance of avoiding excess red blood cell mass in patients. All findings trended towards reversibility after the recovery period. In the 9-month monkey study, the NOAEL was determined to be 3 mg/kg/day (2.4 times the clinical dose based on body surface area), based on the daprodustat-related toxic effects coincident with excess red blood cell mass observed at \ge 10 mg/kg/day (\ge 8 times the clinical dose based on body surface area). The narrow margin (3.3-fold dose-range) between the NOAEL and a significantly toxic dose corroborate the narrow therapeutic index observed in the rat.
L999: Upwards of 150 genes known to be involved in angiogenesis, glucose metabolism, cell proliferation, and inhibition of apoptosis are regulated by HIFs in response to hypoxia (Selvaraju et al. 2014). However, no toxicity studies were conducted in animal models of anemia, and excess hematocrit in healthy animal models confounds identification of toxicity not related to excess erythrocytosis and high blood viscosity. Indeed, risks associated with daprodustat observed in long-term animal toxicology studies appear attributable to polycythemia and related sequelae. While data in non-anemic animals may somewhat overpredict risks of the use of daprodustat in patients with chronic anemia, the steepness of the dose-response curve for toxicity and narrow therapeutic index observed in animals require caution during clinical use.
L1000: Reproductive risks of daprodustat were assessed in a comprehensive battery of studies covering the entire reproductive cycle, including a fertility and early embryonic development study in female rats, embryo-fetal development studies in rats and rabbits, and a pre- and post-natal development study in rats. Adverse developmental effects in offspring observed in rats and rabbits in the fertility and early embryonic development, embryo-fetal development and pre- and post-natal development studies were considered primarily a consequence of maternal toxicity related to excess red blood cell mass. No adverse effects on fertility were observed in male rats. Impacts on fertility in female rats were consistent with the established consequences of maternal toxicity during early pregnancy. These data are presented in Section 8.4, and the reproductive and developmental toxicity findings are discussed in detail in Section 13.2.4. Labeling recommendations are consistent with erythropoietin stimulating agents, as the data suggest risk is related to daprodustat's primary pharmacology (i.e., risks with hematocrit overshoot).
L1001: Daprodustat and its major metabolites were determined not to be genotoxic using in vitro and in vivo assays, and daprodustat was deemed not to pose a significant carcinogenic risk based on a carcinogenicity assessment that included 2-year rat and mouse carcinogenicity studies.
L1002: A juvenile toxicity study was conducted in rats with dosing beginning on post-natal day 4 (generally approximates a full-term human neonate) to evaluate the pharmacological consequence of daprodustat increasing RBC mass during development. The study showed dose-related decreases in body weight/body weight gain in both sexes of young rats and delayed attainment of developmental landmarks in females (e.g., increased the mean age of vaginal patency and increased the estrous cycle length). Minimal decreases in femur length were also noted, which correlated with decreased body weight/body weight gain. Decreased body weight gain and developmental delay is reasonably explained by the impact of excess red blood cell mass in the young, developing non-anemic rat. While the toxicity profile in juvenile animals was qualitatively similar to that observed in adults, younger animals appeared more sensitive than adults (the NOAEL in juvenile rats was below the clinical dose based on body surface area). These data suggest that the use of daprodustat in pediatric patients warrants caution.
L1003: As discussed above, the plasma protein binding of daprodustat is extremely high (approaching 100%) in rat and rabbit, which precluded an accurate estimation of pharmacologically active (free) drug in rat and rabbit plasma for comparison to human free drug levels. Exposure margins (see Table 68) for labeling purposes were therefore derived using body surface area extrapolation. Supporting the use of body surface area extrapolation, this method predicts a 3-fold animal:human safety margin for gastric erosions/ulcers, an imbalance of which occurred in clinical trials. In contrast, the use of the maximum plasma concentration (C_{max}) or the area under the concentration-time curve (AUC) to determine the animal:human exposure multiple appears to grossly overpredict clinical safety (e.g., the use of unadjusted AUC produces a safety margin for gastric erosions/ulcers as high as 845-fold).
L1004: Overall, the nonclinical data support chronic clinical use of daprodustat for the treatment of anemia, but studies consistently demonstrate a narrow therapeutic index with the potential for severe consequences related to hematocrit overshoot. No other outstanding nonclinical safety issues of significant concern were observed at clinically relevant exposures in the nonclinical toxicology program. Therefore, the nonclinical pharmacology/toxicology data support approval of this NDA.
