L2044: ## Key Study Findings
L2045: There were 2 mortalities including one in control group and one in 60 mg/kg/day group with 3X metabolite cocktail (Group 3). The cause of death was not determined at the necropsy for the control animal or the female in the 60 mg/kg/day + 3X metabolite group, however this female lost 12 g of body weight from GD 20 to 21. Another 60 mg/kg/day + 3X metabolite GSK12788763A-treated animal was prematurely terminated due to cannibalism of the F1 litter (7/13).
L2046: Daprodustat-related effects were observed at 60 mg/kg/day with decreased mean maternal body weight gain during late gestation of 44% or 60%, Group 2 and 3, respectively. Decreases of 30% and 40% were also observed at 40 mg/kg/day without (Group 6) and with (Group 7) 1X metabolite cocktail. Decreases in body weight compared to controls for 40 and 60 mg/kg/day corresponded with decreased mean food consumption. Mean body weight gain/body weight loss persisted at 60 mg/kg/day with decreased food consumption during the lactation period (53% or 90% compared to controls, Group 2 and 3, respectively) but the effects on body weight or food consumption at 40 mg/kg/day resolved during LD 1 to 7.
L2047: In addition, there were increases in the duration of parturition of 16.8 and 20 min/pup, Group 2 and 3, respectively, at 60 mg/kg/day compared to controls mean of 6 minutes/pup. The increase of stillborn pups and found dead/missing (presumed cannibalized) pups decreased mean pup survival and litter sizes by LD 7 (22% decrease compared to control) at 60 mg/kg/day, and decreased pup body weight up to ~30% from birth to PND 7 were also observed at 60 mg/kg/day. The findings at 40 mg/kg/day were similar to that of 60 mg/kg/day with slightly less severity and trend of reversibility.
L2048: The NOAEL was defined at 10 mg/kg/day with C_{max} 72.4 µg/mL and AUC_{0-t} µg.h/mL, based on maternal toxicity and reduced embryo-fetal survival at the next highest dose of 40 mg/kg/day, suggesting metabolite levels may impact maternal toxicity and associated embryo-fetal toxicity.
L2049: ## **Title/ Study Number:** GSK1278863A + Metabolites [GSK2391220A (M2), GSK2506104A (M3) and GSK2531401A (M13)]: Oral Gavage and Subcutaneous Injection Pre- and Postnatal Development Study in Rats/2018N365151/00
L2050: ## **Key Study Findings**
L2051: - There was one mortality in the F0 generation at the HD of 40 mg/kg/day that appears daprodustat-related, 2 mortalities of unclear relationship, and 1 mortality that were considered unrelated.
- Body weight gain during LD 1 to 4 was lower in HD with corresponding lower food consumption during GD 18-21 and LD 4-8 compared to controls.
- The daprodustat-related lower survival of F1 generation was statistically significant and noted based on the lower viability index on PND 1 to 4, smaller live litter size on PND 4 and 21, and increased number of dead pups on PND 2 to 4.
- Slightly longer delivery time was noted in HD (3/24) compared to controls.
- The systemic exposure to daprodustat in F0 generation rats increased as the dose increased in a less than dose proportional manner and metabolites (M2, M3, or M13) were detected in plasma at similar levels across the doses between GD 9 and LD 21.
- There was daprodustat detected in F1 generation suckling pups, which suggests the secretion of daprodustat into milk.
- The maternal body weight gain of F1 generation was lower in HD (40 mg/kg/day) females during gestation and lactation compared to controls.
- Effects (e.g., reduced litter size) at the HD on the F2 generation fell within the historical control range and were deemed not daprodustat-related.
- NOAEL is determined at 7 mg/kg/day, based on maternal toxicity and reduced embryo-fetal survival at the next highest dose of 40 mg/kg/day.

L2094: ## F1 Generation (Postweaning)
L2095: Mortality	One LD (0.8 mg/kg/day) male was found dead on PND 69.
Body weights	The body weight gains of HD rats during PND 22-29 were lower in F1 generation males (9%) and females (8%) with statistical significance compared to controls.
Maternal mean body weight gain of F1 generation was lower at HD (40 mg/mg/kg) during gestation (GD 15-21) and 75% lower body weight gain on Lactation Days 1-7 was noted compared to controls with statistical significance.
Clinical signs	Daprodustat-related dehydration and whole-body cold to touch were observed (18 pups in 3 litters and 15 pups in 2 litters, respectively) in the preweaning period.
HD (40 mg/kg/day) rats presented localized swelling along the surface of the abdomen starting from PND 53 (females) and PND 71 (males), and this finding was not reversed until termination.
Sexual maturation	No drug-related findings observed.
Noteworthy findings include vaginal patency delayed by 0.9 day (statistically significant) and lower mean number of implantations by 9% at HD of 40 mg/kg/day compared to controls. These changes were within the historical control data range.
In males, there was no daprodustat-related effect on spermatogenesis in testes based on the qualitative evaluation of spermatogenesis with normal progression of spermatogenic cycle.

L2110: ## 13.2.5. Juvenile Toxicology
L2111: ## Title/ Study Number: GSK1278863A: Oral Juvenile Toxicity Study in Rats/ 2020N436444/00
L2112: ## Key Study Findings
L2113: - At the MD and HD, there were daprodustat-related increases in the mean age of vaginal patency considered secondary to decreased mean body weight/body weight gain. At the HD, there was also increased estrous cycle length in females, considered secondary to the effects on growth and the early evaluation of estrous cycles (PND 57 vs. 63 to 70).
- Statistically significant increased RBC mass was observed at the HD.
- Minimal decrease in femur length was noted at HD at the end of dosing period but the decrease did not resolve in males and worsened in females at the end of recovery period. This effect corresponded with decreased body weight gain at this dose, where females had decreased mean body weight compared to controls through PND 43.
L2114: - Daprodustat-related findings of increased cellularity in the bone marrow of sternum and extramedullary hematopoiesis in the spleen were observed at HD at the end of dosing. The NOAEL is at LD of 2/0.8 mg/kg/day.

L2123: **Table 173. Observations and Results of Oral Juvenile Toxicity Study in Rats/ 2020N436444/00**
L2124: Parameter	Major Findings
Mortality	There were 13 deaths observed (found dead, euthanized due to moribundity, or presumed to be cannibalized), but only one death at MD that appeared to be drug-related (dehydration and body weight loss with no evidence of trauma or gavage error). There were no dose dependency and mortalities were even observed in controls, therefore no mortalities could be clearly attributed to daprodustat in this study.
Clinical signs	Dose-related dehydration at MD (1/30) and HD (4/30) during dosing period was observed.
Body weights/Body weight gain	Transient lower body weight gain (6-15%) was observed at the MD and HD between PND 4 and 32, and the body weights were comparable between the control and drug treatment groups by the end of dosing period. Changes in BWG was not correlated with decreased food consumption.
BWG decrease persisted in MD and HD females with lower BWG (17% and 20%, respectively) during the recovery period (PND 71-155),
L2125: Parameter	Major Findings
Developmental hallmarks
Sexual maturity and Estrous cycling Assessment	
The findings were not direct effect from drug but likely secondary to mean body weight effects.
Dose dependent increase in mean age of vaginal patency by 1.7 and 3.1 days, at MD and HD, respectively, was observed which were within the historical control data range (29.3-34.1 days but were considered secondary to decreased mean BW/BWG.
The mean estrous cycle length of 4.6 days was increased at HD by 0.4 days compared to controls. The increase was outside the historical control data range (4.2-4.3 days).
Increase in number of females (4/20) in continuous (6 or more days) diestrus was noted. The increase was outside the historical control data range of 3 females/study, but within a range observed previously by the testing facility.
No drug-related effects were observed in balano-preputial separation in males.

Neurobehavioral testing	No drug-related effects were observed in FOD, Acoustic startle habituation, Motor activity, and Morris water maze tests.
Ophthalmology	No drug-related effects were observed.
Hematology	
Daprodustat-related increase in RBC mass, reticulocyte and decrease in platelet were observed:
During the dosing period on PND 35, the PCV (%) increased by 20% (male) and 23% (female) at HD with statistical significance (p\le 0.01).
At the end of dosing period on PND 64, increases in RBC, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and reticulocyte counts and decrease in platelet were observed in HD animals.
At the end of recovery period on PND 160, the change in hematology parameters resolved except the increase in RBC count (11%) in HD males and decrease in platelet count (12%) in HD females.

Coagulation	Prolongation of APTT at HD (8%↑ in males, 21%↑ in females) with decrease in fibrinogen (24%↓ in males, 25%↓ in females) were observed at the end of dosing PND 64, which resolved at the end of recovery period on PND 160. This finding is likely daprodustat-related.
Clinical chemistry	Drug-related decrease in total cholesterol by 23% in HD males and 29% in HD females and increase in triglycerides 151% in HD males were observed with statistical significance (p\le 0.01) at the end of dosing on PND 64. This finding resolved at the end of recovery period on PND 160.
Urinalysis	No daprodustat-related findings noted.
Organ weights	No daprodustat-related findings noted.
Femur length	
Minimal decrease in femur length of HD males and females (0.97X and 0.98X controls, respectively) was noted at the end of dosing period (PND 64).
After the recovery period (PND159), the decrease of femur length remained minimal (0.97X control) in HD males but worsened in the HD females (0.95X controls, p\le 0.01).

Macroscopic findings	No daprodustat-related findings noted.
L2126: Parameter	Major Findings
Microscopic findings	
Increased cellularity in the bone marrow of sternum and incidence and/or severity of extramedullary hematopoiesis in the spleen were observed at HD at the end of dosing period (PND 64). The Applicant explains that the increased cells in the bone marrow and spleen were predominately of the erythroid lineage. This finding is likely from the pharmacological effect of drug increasing hematopoiesis.
Dilatation of the kidney was noted at low incidence in daprodustat-treated males at ≥ 2/0.8 mg/kg/day.
Increased hepatocellular vacuolation was observed in HD females.

Toxicokinetic	
Minimal focal epidermal hyperplasia of the skin was noted in one HD female.
Daprodustat was detected in plasma. The systemic exposure (AUC0-24hr and Cmax) increased with dose increment and the increase was less than dose-proportional. The daprodustat levels were maintained through PND 63 and peaked at PND 21 despite lowering the doses, although dosing was more frequent.
There was no evidence of gender difference (< 2-fold) in systemic exposure to daprodustat. The Tmax ranged between 1.5 – 12 hours, with increased Tmax on PND 12 (dose dependent).

L2162: M2 and M3 were not genotoxic in the presence or absence of metabolic activation for both 3 and 24 hour treatment. L2172: **Title / Study Number:** 2011N124885/00/ GSK2531401A: Intravenous Liver Comet Assay in Crl:CD1(Icr) Mice
L2173: ## Key Study Findings
L2174: Male Crl:CD1 (ICR) mice (n=5-6/group) were treated with 2 intravenous (IV) doses of 0 (0.9% (w/v) aqueous sodium chloride), 25, 100, 200, or 300 mg/kg GSK2531401A (Metabolite 13; M13), approximately 21 hours apart with a single harvest 3 hours after the last dose. One oral gavage dose of 30 mg/kg Ethyl Methane-Sulfonate (EMS) was used as positive control. 4 independent studies were conducted; however, due to a technical failure of the electrophoresis procedure, the Comet data for one study were invalidated and have not been reported.
L2175: Mice given 300 mg/kg M13 convulsed and died immediately following dosing. A mild increase in alanine aminotransferase activity was observed in 3/6 mice given 200 mg/kg/day. In these mice, a corresponding minimal increase in aspartate aminotransferase activity was also noted. Highest individual values in this group (no. 102) were 265 and 263 U/L for alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase, respectively. M13 was negative at 25 or 100 mg/kg/day across 3 independent studies. Increase of % Tail DNA was evident at the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) 200 mg/kg/day GSK2531401A (M13). But the positive result was not reproducible across 3 independent studies. Therefore, the result of Comet assay is equivocal.

L2193: ## **Carcinogenicity Study**
L2194: ## **Title/ Study Number: GSK1278863A: A 2-Year Oral (gavage) Carcinogenicity Study in Rats/ 2014n196080**
L2195: ## **Key Study Findings**
L2196: A daprodustat-related neoplastic finding was observed. The incidence of fibroadenoma in the mammary gland at HD (4 mg/kg/day) in males was statistically significant and the incidence rate was approximately 13% which exceeds the historical control data range (maximum incidence rate 6.52%). However, the incidence of the combination of adenoma and fibroadenoma in the mammary gland was not statistically significant. Regardless of the daprodustat-related fibroadenoma findings in males, the clinical relevance of fibroadenoma in the mammary gland of males is considered to be low.

L2213: ## 14. Clinical Pharmacology
L2214: ## 14.1. In Vitro Studies
L2215: ## 14.1.1. Plasma protein binding
L2216: ## Plasma Protein Binding of Daprodustat
L2217: In a study to determine the extent of the binding of daprodustat to plasma proteins from mouse, rat, rabbit, dog, monkey, and human pooled plasma (3 subjects/pooled sample), plasma samples were incubated, using equilibrium dialysis, at daprodustat concentrations of 0.2, 1, 10 and 50 µg/mL [Report CD2010/00340]. In addition, the protein binding of daprodustat to human serum albumin (HSA) (0.600mM) or α1-acid glycoprotein (AAG) (0.015 and 0.150mM) was determined using equilibrium dialysis at daprodustat concentrations of 0.2, 1, 10 and 30 µg/mL.
L2218: The binding of daprodustat to plasma protein was high in all species evaluated (generally &gt;98%), specifically in human, 99.4% at the three low test concentrations, and 98.3% at 50 µg/mL. Binding was also high to HSA (&gt;99.3%), while low to AAG (&lt;20%). In general, there was no evidence of concentration-dependent protein binding of daprodustat in all species over the concentration range evaluated.
L2219: ## Plasma Protein Binding of Metabolites of Daprodustat
L2220: In a study to determine the extent of human plasma protein binding for the six predominant circulating human metabolites of daprodustat [M2 (GSK2391220), M3 (GSK2531403 and GSK2506104), M4 (GSK2499166), M5 (GSK2531399), M6 (GSK2531398), and M13 (GSK2531400 and GSK2531401)], pooled human plasma was obtained from three non-fasted
L2221: male donors [2012N131897]. Binding was determined by equilibrium dialysis at concentrations of 10, 100, 250 and 500 ng/mL and were incubated for 18 hours. Concentrations of each metabolite were determined by ultra-performance liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectroscopy (UPLC-MS/MS). The plasma protein binding of M2, M3 (both enantiomers), M6, and M13 (both enantiomers) was determined to be low, less than 34% for each metabolite across concentrations. There was no evidence of concentration-dependent protein binding of M2, M3, M6, and M13 over the range evaluated. The plasma protein binding of M4 and M5 was determined to be lower (68 and 74%, respectively) at the lowest test concentration (10 ng/mL) and increased with increasing concentrations up to ~98%, suggesting concentration-dependent protein binding of M4 and M5 over the concentration range evaluated.
L2222: ## 14.1.2. Distribution in red blood cells
L2223: The in vitro blood cell association of daprodustat was determined in blood (a single human plasma sample) by adding daprodustat at concentrations of 1.0 and 10 µg/mL (n=3/concentration/species, 0.5% (v/v) DMSO) after incubation for 30 minutes. All quantitative analysis was by LC-MS/MS. There was generally minimal association of daprodustat with blood cells in vitro with blood/plasma ratios of 1.23 and 0.75 at 1.0 and 10 µg/mL, respectively.
L2224: ## 14.1.3. Metabolism studies
L2225: ## Oxidative Enzymology in Human Liver Microsomes
L2226: The oxidative enzymology of [^{14}C]daprodustat (5µM) was investigated using pooled human liver microsomes and rh-CYP enzymes (Supersomes^{\text{TM}}). Human liver microsomes from mixed-gender pools of 15 human livers were used. Inhibition of daprodustat metabolism was investigated by incubating [^{14}C]daprodustat with human liver microsomes in the presence and absence of the selective CYP inhibitors: azamulin, sulphaphenazole, quinidine, montelukast, furafylline, and benzylnirvanol (inhibitors of CYP3A4, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, CYP2C8, CYP2C19, CYP1A2, respectively). Supersomes contained individually over-expressed rh-CYP enzymes (CYP1A2, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6 and CYP3A4) derived from baculovirus infected insect cells. [^{14}C]daprodustat incubations with pooled human liver microsomes or recombinant CYP enzymes were conducted. The reactions were started by the addition of an NADPH regenerating system. The supernatants from [^{14}C] GSK1278863 incubations with human liver microsomes or recombinant CYP enzymes were analyzed by radio-HPLC. [^{14}C]daprodustat was metabolized in human liver microsomes to three metabolites, M8, M9/M22, and M10 (mono-oxidation). An additional NADPH-dependent radio-peak was detected in incubations with human liver microsomes. This peak was not detected by LC/MS and therefore was not structurally characterized, but its rate of formation was calculated. These metabolites, which constituted 95% of the total radioactivity, were inhibited by montelukast, a selective CYP2C8 inhibitor. [^{14}C]daprodustat was metabolized to M2, M3, M4, M5, M6, M7, M8, M9/M22, M10, and M17, in human recombinant CYP2C8 incubations. Metabolites M2 through M7 (di-oxidation) were not detected in human liver microsomes. In human recombinant CYP3A4 incubations only M8 and M9/M22 were formed but turnover was low and only constituted 5% turnover. There were no metabolites detected in incubations with recombinant CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19 or
L2227: CYP2D6. The data from human liver microsomes with selective inhibitors and scaled results from recombinant human CYP enzymes suggest that CYP2C8 is the primary CYP enzyme involved in the oxidative metabolism of daprodustat in vitro with a minor contribution by CYP3A4.
L2228: ## Induction of CYP Enzymes in Human Hepatocytes
L2229: The effects of daprodustat (0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0, 10, 30 and 100\muM) on the mRNA levels of CYP1A2, 2B6 and 3A4 were evaluated in cultured human hepatocytes from three donors after exposure to daprodustat for 48 hours. The mRNA level for each specific CYP was determined using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction technology (TaqManTM). No notable increases in the mean mRNA levels of CYP1A2, CYP2B6 or CYP3A4 were observed. Minor reductions in mRNA levels (ratio of treated over control &lt;0.5) were apparent for CYP1A2 at 100\muM and CYP3A4 at all concentrations tested and the decreases in mRNA level observed may not be associated with hepatocyte health because no decreases in total RNA and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) were observed. Treatment with daprodustat caused no notable increases in the mean mRNA levels of CYP1A2, CYP2B6 or CYP3A4 within the concentration range examined.
L2230: ## Inhibition of CYP Enzymes in Human Microsomes
L2231: The potential of daprodustat to inhibit CYP1A2, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6 or 3A4 in a concentration-dependent or metabolism dependent manner was investigated in vitro with human liver microsomes and using selective probe substrates in the presence and absence of daprodustat (0.1 to 100\muM). For concentration-dependent inhibition (half maximal inhibitory concentration [IC50] determination), daprodustat (0.1 to 100\muM) was pre-incubated with human liver microsomal protein and the respective probe substrates (at a final concentration approximating the Km) with NADPH (NADP+, glucose-6-phosphate and glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase) generating system was added to start the reactions. The selective probe substrates used in the presence and absence of daprodustat were: hydroxylation of phenacetin (1A2); 4-hydroxylation of diclofenac (2C9); 4-hydroxylation of S-mephentoin (2C19); 1-hydroxylation of bufuralol (2D6); 1-hydroxylation of midazolam, oxidation of nifedipine and o-hydroxylation of atorvastatin (3A4). The reactions to measure metabolism-dependent inhibition were carried out in the presence and absence of NADPH.
L2232: The potential for daprodustat to inhibit the major human CYPs was low in human liver microsomes with all IC50 values &gt;100\muM. In addition, daprodustat did not display any metabolism-dependent inhibition in human liver microsome CYP1A2, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6 or 3A4-nifedipine assays.
L2233: ## 14.1.4. Transporter interaction studies
L2234: ## P-glycoprotein Transport and Membrane Permeability
L2235: ## P-gp Substrate Potential and Permeability
L2236: The P-gp substrate activity and intrinsic apparent permeability of daprodustat were evaluated in Madin Darby canine kidney (MCDK) cells transfected with the human multi-drug resistant 1
L2237: gene (hMDR1) [Report UH2008/00018]. Bidirectional [apical-to-basolateral (A→B) and basolateral-to-apical (B→A)] transport of daprodustat (5µM) was studied across MDCKII-hMDR1 cell monolayers in the absence and presence of GF120918 (P-gp inhibitor at 2µM). The apical efflux ratio was defined as the ratio of unidirectional transmonolayer flux of test compound across the cell monolayers from the basolateral to apical (B→A) compartment divided by that of the same compound from the A→B compartment. An apical efflux ratio &gt;2 for a compound suggests P-gp-mediated transport. Daprodustat was not a substrate of human P-gp in vitro, as the apical efflux ratio was ~1 in the absence or presence of GF120918 in MDCKII-hMDR1 cell monolayers.
L2238: ## Passive Membrane Permeability
L2239: A study was conducted to determine the passive membrane permeability and the absorptive membrane permeability of daprodustat using bio-relevant buffer [fasted state simulated intestinal fluid (FaSSIF)] in MDCKII-hMDR1 cells in the presence of the potent P-gp inhibitor, GF120918 [Report CD2008/00421]. The passive membrane permeability of [^{14}C]daprodustat (3µM) was determined at pH 7.4, and the absorptive membrane permeability of [^{14}C]daprodustat (3µM) was determined at pH 5.5 and 7.4 to simulate conditions in the gastro-intestinal tract. Permeabilities were measured using MDCKII-hMDR1 cell monolayers in the presence of GF120918.
L2240: [^{14}C]daprodustat was determined to have moderate passive membrane permeability of 21 nm/s at pH 7.4. The absorptive membrane permeabilities of [^{14}C]daprodustat in the presence of FaSSIF were both high at pH 7.4 and pH 5.5 with a P7.4[abs] value of 191 nm/s and a P5.5[abs] value of 325 nm/s. The presence of biorelevant buffer, FaSSIF, increased the permeability of daprodustat. In addition, daprodustat permeability is increased at pH 5.5 (Table 183).

L2249: ## P-gp Transport Inhibition
L2250: Daprodustat was evaluated as an in vitro inhibitor of human P-gp [Report CD2008/00669]. Inhibition of P-gp-mediated transport of digoxin (0.03µM) by daprodustat (0.1 to 100µM) was investigated by determining the basolateral to apical ([B→A]) transport of [^{3}H]digoxin by MDCKII-hMDR1 cells transfected with the human MDR1 gene, which express the P-gp protein. Daprodustat did not inhibit transport of digoxin via human P-gp.
L2251: ## Evaluation as Human BCRP Substrate
L2252: The bi-directional transport of daprodustat (3µM) was investigated using MDCKII-breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) cells transfected with the human BCRP gene and heterologously
L2253: expressing human BCRP protein [Report 2015N237800]. Assessments were made in the presence and absence of the BCRP inhibitor, GF120918. After 90 minutes of incubation, samples were analyzed by liquid scintillation counting or LC-MS/MS. A compound is classified as a BCRP substrate if the apical efflux ratio in the absence of inhibitor GF120918 is \ge 2 and this efflux collapses to \sim 1 in the presence of inhibitor, GF120918. The apical efflux ratio of daprodustat at 3\mu\text{M} was determined as 4.4 and 0.65 in the absence and presence of GF120918, respectively, in the MDCKII-BCRP cell line. Thus, daprodustat is a substrate of human BCRP with an efflux ratio of 4.4 at a concentration of 3\mu\text{M}.

L2260: ## OATP1B1 and OAT1B3 Substrate Potential
L2261: To evaluate the substrate potential of daprodustat and its six predominant circulating human metabolites; M2 (GSK2391220), M3 (GSK2506104), M4 (GSK2487818), M5 (GSK2506102), M6 (GSK2531398) and M13 (GSK2531401), the time-dependent transport of daprodustat and metabolites (0.01 to 10\mu\text{M}) in OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporter expressing Human Embryonic Kidney (HEK-293) cells was measured by LC-MS/MS [Report 2015N255319].
L2262: Daprodustat was a substrate of OATP1B1 but was not a substrate of OATP1B3. M13 was not a substrate of OATP1B1 but was a substrate of OATP1B3. M2, M4, M5, and M6 were substrates of the OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. M3 was not a substrate of OATP1B1 nor OATP1B3.
L2263: ## Inhibition of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3

Cells were incubated for 5 minutes for OATP1B1 and 10 minutes for OATP1B3. For analysis of total radioactivity, the contents of each well were determined by liquid scintillation counting in glass vials containing scintillant.
L2265: Daprodustat inhibited OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 with calculated IC50 values of 6\mu\text{M} and 11\mu\text{M}, respectively.

L2276: In a study to determine if the six predominant circulating human metabolites of daprodustat [M2 (GSK2391220), M3 (GSK2531403), M4 (GSK2487818), M5 (GSK2506102), M6 (GSK2531398) and M13 (GSK2531401)] are inhibitors of the human OATP1B1, transport inhibition of fluorescein labelled methotrexate via the OATP1B1 (expressed in HEK-MSRII cells after transduction of a BacMam baculovirus coding for OATP1B1) was evaluated after the incubation with each metabolite (0.085 to 50\muM, n=8) [Report 2013N166580]. Metabolites M2, M3, M4, M5, M6 and M13 did not inhibit human OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 at concentrations \le50\muM.
L2277: ## Substrate Potential With OAT1, OAT3, OCT2, MATE1 and MATE2-K
L2278: In a study to evaluate the potential of daprodustat and six predominant circulating human metabolites of daprodustat [M2 (GSK2391220), M3 (GSK2506104), M4 (GSK2487818), M5 (GSK2506102), M6 (GSK2531398) and M13 (GSK2531401)] to act as substrates of OAT1, OAT3, OCT2, MATE1 and MATE2-K, the substrate potential of each test article was determined by measuring the time-dependent uptake of the test article in transporter expressing and control cells (S2 cells for OAT1 and OAT3; HEK-293 cell for OCT2, MATE1 and MATE2-K) [Report 2015N249257]. After incubating each test article with the various transporter expressing cells, the cells were washed and quantity of each test article associated with the cells was measured by LC-MS/MS. Daprodustat, M4, M5 and M6 were not substrates of the transporters OAT1, OAT3, OCT2, MATE1 and MATE2-K. M3 and M13 were substrates of OAT3, but not of OAT1, OCT2, MATE1 and MATE2-K. M2 was a weak substrate of OAT1 and OAT3, but not of OCT2, MATE1 and MATE2-K.
L2279: ## Inhibition of OAT1, OAT3, OCT2, MATE1 and MATE2-K
L2280: In a study to evaluate daprodustat and six predominant circulating human metabolites of daprodustat [M2 (GSK2391220), M3 (GSK2506104), M4 (GSK2487818), M5 (GSK2506102), M6 (GSK2531398) and M13 (GSK2531401)] for inhibition of the OAT1 and OAT3, OCT2 and MATE1 and MATE2-K (expressed in solute carrier (SLC) transporter expressing cells (S2) (OAT1 or OAT3) or HEK-293 cells (OCT2, MATE1 or MATE2-K)) activity of each transporter was measured by liquid scintillation counting (LSC) using respective radiolabeled probe
L2281: substrates in the absence or presence of an inhibitor cocktail at a single concentration of each (daprodustat, 1.4\muM; M2, 20\muM; M3, 20\muM; M4, 10\muM; M5, 5\muM; M6, 10\muM and M13, 10\muM) [Report 2015N242070]. Daprodustat and its six predominant circulating human metabolites (M2, M3, M4, M5, M6 and M13) did not inhibit OAT1, OAT3, OCT2, MATE1, and MATE2-K-mediated transport of each respective probe substrate.
L2282: ## Daprodustat Uptake by Human Hepatocytes
L2283: In a study to investigate the transport processes involved in the in vitro hepatic uptake of daprodustat (0.5 and 0.3\muM) using cryopreserved human hepatocytes from 3 different donors, uptake experiments were conducted in the presence and absence of an inhibitor cocktail [Report 2015N232657]. Incubations performed in the presence of inhibitor cocktail were used to determine the passive uptake of daprodustat into the human hepatocytes. The inhibitor cocktail included the rifamycin SV and cyclosporine A (inhibitors of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3), montelukast (inhibitor of OATP2B1) and imipramine (inhibitor of OCT1). [^{3}H]estradiol glucuronide ([^{3}H]EG) (0.02\muM) was used as positive control substrate in a separate set of incubations under the conditions stated. Daprodustat uptake in cryopreserved human hepatocytes from 3 different donors, at 0.5 or 0.3\muM, was not inhibited by the inhibitor cocktail, suggesting a primarily passive process is involved. Uptake of [^{3}H]EG was inhibited by the inhibitor cocktail, with a signal-to-noise ratio between 3.4 and 7.9, demonstrating functionality of the cell system. There was no notable difference (\ge2-fold) in daprodustat transport into cryopreserved human hepatocytes in the presence of prototypical inhibitors (cyclosporine A, rifamycin, montelukast, and imipramine) of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OATP2B1 or OCT1 transporters, suggesting that daprodustat is not a substrate of these transporters.
L2284: ## M4 Uptake by Human Hepatocytes
L2285: In a study to investigate the time dependent, active uptake in the in vitro hepatic uptake of daprodustat metabolite M4 (GSK2487818) (0.2, 2 and 15\muM) using pooled cryopreserved human hepatocytes, uptake experiments were conducted in the presence and absence of an inhibitor cocktail [Report 2015N259558]. Incubations performed in the presence of inhibitor cocktail were used to determine the passive uptake of M4 into the human hepatocytes. The inhibitor cocktail included the rifamycin SV and imipramine. [^{3}H]estradiol glucuronide ([^{3}H]EG) (0.02\muM) was used as positive control substrate in a separate set of incubations under the conditions stated. M4 uptake in cryopreserved pooled human hepatocytes at 15\muM was not inhibited by the inhibitor cocktail, suggesting a primarily passive process is involved. Uptake of [^{3}H]EG was inhibited by the inhibitor cocktail, with a signal to noise ratio of 3.8 to 4.2, demonstrating functionality of the cell system. There was no notable difference (\ge2-fold) in M4 transport into pooled cryopreserved human hepatocytes in the presence of prototypical inhibitors (rifamycin, and imipramine) of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OATP2B1 or OCT1 transporters, suggesting that M4 is not a substrate of these transporters in a qualified physiologically relevant system.
L2286: ## 14.2. In Vivo Studies
L2287: ## Single Dose in Renal Impairment Subjects (Study PH112843)
L2288: **Title:** A Phase I, single-dose, randomized and single-blind (Part 1) fixed sequence and open-label (Part 2), study to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of GSK1278863A in subjects with renal impairment and matched healthy volunteers.
L2289: **Study Design:** This was a single-center, Phase I, 2-part study. Part 1 was conducted in subjects with moderate (Stage 3; eGFR 30 to 59 mL/min/1.73 m2) to severe (Stage 4; eGFR 15 to 29 mL/min/1.73 m2) renal impairment (Cohort 1) and subjects with normal renal function (eGFR ≥90 mL/min/1.73 m2; Cohort 2) and employed a single-dose, 2-period crossover, randomized sequence, with daprodustat dose levels of 50 and 150 mg. Part 2 was conducted in subjects with hemodialysis-dependent renal impairment (Stage 5; eGFR &lt;15 mL/min/1.73 m2; Cohort 3) and employed a single-dose, 2-period, fixed sequence, open-label design. During Part 2, study drug was administered before dialysis in Period 1 and post-dialysis in Period 2, with a single daprodustat dose of 150 mg in both periods. Blood samples from the arterial and venous side of the circulation were compared at fixed timepoints following dosing during an active dialysis session (Period 1) to evaluate the effect of dialysis on daprodustat plasma concentrations.
L2290: Treatment periods for both Part 1 and Part 2 were separated by a 7 to 10-day washout period. Biomarkers associated with erythropoiesis, namely EPO, reticulocyte count, hemoglobin (Hb), Hct, RBC, and hepcidin as well as markers related iron metabolism and utilization, including serum ferritin, TIBC, and UIBC, were also assessed. VEGF was also measured in this study. Pharmacodynamic (PD) assessments occurred out to 48 hours post-dose.
L2291: ## Results and Conclusions
L2292: ## Pharmacokinetics
L2293: Daprodustat pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters in subjects with Stages 3 to 4 (moderate to severe) renal impairment and their matched healthy subjects are similar. Daprodustat exposure [AUC(0-inf)] increased in a dose-proportional manner for the 50 and 150 mg doses. There were no marked differences in daprodustat PK between subjects with moderate to severe renal impairment (Cohort 1) and matched healthy subjects (Cohort 2). Daprodustat PK was similar in hemodialysis subjects (Cohort 3) on a non-dialysis day and subjects with moderate to severe renal impairment (Cohort 1). In HDD subjects (Cohort 3), plasma daprodustat exposures tended to be higher during an active dialysis session compared to those observed on the day without dialysis, indicating a reduction in the clearance of daprodustat during the dialysis procedure. There were no consistent differences in daprodustat concentrations between the arterial and venous samples, suggesting daprodustat was not significantly cleared by hemodialysis.

L2298: ## Pharmacodynamics
L2299: Rapid, dose-dependent increases were observed in mean EPO concentrations in all cohorts following dosing in Period 1, with approximately 3- to 10-fold greater increases observed in subjects with renal impairment (Cohorts 1 and 3) as compared to normal healthy subjects. In Cohort 3, EPO concentrations were higher in Period 1 as compared to Period 2, which may be function of the higher plasma concentrations observed in these subjects during the dialysis period as compared to the period without dialysis. At 48 hours post-dose, EPO concentrations in the healthy subjects (Cohort 2) had returned to near-baseline levels, but remained elevated above baseline concentrations in subjects with renal impairment and hemodialysis subjects.
L2300: Mean total RBC counts were similar between the 3 cohorts at baseline and increased slightly in all cohorts at 24 and 48 hours post-dose during Period 1. Total RBC in healthy subjects
L2301: (Cohort 2) and hemodialysis subjects (Cohort 3) returned to baseline levels at the beginning of Period 2 but remained elevated in subjects with renal impairment (Cohort 1). Mean hemoglobin concentrations in subjects with renal impairment (Cohort 1) increased gradually over time. In healthy subjects (Cohort 2), mean Hb concentrations increased following dosing in both periods, but no obvious dose-related trends were observed. In hemodialysis subjects (Cohort 3), small increases in mean Hb concentrations were noted at 24 hours following dosing in Period 1, but levels returned to baseline at the follow-up assessment.
L2302: ## Repeat Dose (14 Days) in Renal Impairment Subjects (Study PH1115573)
L2303: **Study Title:** A repeat-dose, open-label, parallel-group study to assess the pharmacokinetics of daprodustat and metabolites in normal subjects and subjects with impaired renal function.
L2304: **Study Design:** This was a repeat-dose, parallel-group study in subjects with normal renal function, non-hemodialysis subjects with renal impairment (Stages 3/4/5 CKD), and hemodialysis subjects with Stage 5 CKD. All subjects received a 5 mg daprodustat dose once daily for 14 days (normal renal function and non-hemodialysis subjects) or 15 days (hemodialysis subjects). Blood samples were collected on Days 1 and 14 for all subjects and additionally on Day 15 for hemodialysis subjects to allow for collection on dialysis and non-dialysis days. EPO and hepcidin were also assessed.
L2305: ## Results and Conclusions
L2306: ## Pharmacokinetics
L2307: Daprodustat exposure (AUC_{0-\infty} and C_{max}) following single and/or repeat doses was not clinically different in subjects with normal renal function (190 ng.h/mL and 93 ng/mL, respectively), subjects with Stage 3/4 non-dialysis (ND) CKD (176 ng.h/mL and 75 ng/mL), or subjects with Stage 5 hemodialysis CKD on a dialysis day [213 ng.h/mL and 74 ng/mL] and on a non-dialysis day [188 ng.h/mL and 76 ng/mL]. The steady-state C_{max} of daprodustat was 18 to 21% lower in all subjects with renal impairment. Overall, the PK of daprodustat was not meaningfully affected by hemodialysis.
L2308: The major circulating metabolites, defined as \ge 10\% drug-related material (DRM; equal to AUC of metabolite divided by the sum of AUC of all metabolites and parent) in plasma, were M2, M3, and M13 in all populations assessed.
L2309: Daprodustat was not substantially eliminated by the kidney or dialysis, while elimination of its metabolites, being more polar than parent drug, was more susceptible to changes in renal function and dialysis. Dialysis clearance (CLd) values for daprodustat were 7.61 and 7.00 mL/min at 3 and 4 h post-dose, respectively, with negligible extraction ratios, while metabolite CLd values at 3 and 4 h post-dose ranged from 140 to 167 mL/min with extraction ratios &gt;0.42.
L2310: Daprodustat did not accumulate in subjects with normal renal function, subjects with Stage 3/4 ND, or hemodialysis Stage 5 CKD subjects. At steady state, daprodustat was highly bound to plasma protein (percent protein bound &gt;99\%) in all subject groups. The plasma protein binding of M4 and M5 was lower (\sim 31 to 41\% at the 3-hour time point) in subjects
L2311: with renal impairment compared to healthy subjects (~45 and 55%). This may be due to loss of protein in urine, which is common with CKD.
L2312: For subjects with Stage 3/4 ND and Stage 5 hemodialysis CKD (dialysis day), exposure parameter values (AUC and C_{max}) of all daprodustat predominant metabolites were higher than in subjects with normal renal function (Table 187). The exception to this was for metabolites M4, M6 and M13 where a slightly lower C_{max} was observed for subjects with Stage 5 hemodialysis CKD (dialysis day). Subjects with Stage 5 hemodialysis CKD on a non-dialysis day had the highest metabolite exposure. Lower AUC and C_{max} values for the predominant metabolites were observed on a dialysis day compared to a non-dialysis day; however, the apparent t_{1/2} were comparable between the 2 cohorts (except for metabolite M13, which was longer on a dialysis day), indicative of dialysis clearance of metabolites.
L2313: For subjects with Stage 3/4 ND and Stage 5 hemodialysis CKD (dialysis day), the higher exposure and reduced elimination of metabolites results in accumulation for most metabolites (accumulation ratios [Rac] up to 1.4-fold in subjects with Stage 3/4 ND; for Stage 5 CKD, accumulation ratios were calculated based on half-life estimates to be up to 1.8-fold and 1.4-fold for dialysis day and non-dialysis day, respectively, except for M13, for which Rac values were 2.6-fold and 1.5-fold, respectively). No apparent time dependencies from single-dose to multiple-dose administration were observed for any predominant metabolite.

L2319: ## Pharmacodynamics
L2320: In Stage 3/4 ND CKD subjects and Stage 5 hemodialysis CKD subjects, mean EPO concentrations increased from baseline and reached a maximum at 8 to 12 h post-dose and returned approximately to baseline levels at 24 h post-dose. In Stage 3/4 CKD subjects, the maximum observed increase in EPO on Day 14 occurred at 8 hours post-dose and was ~2.4-fold the pre-dose value on Day 14. In Stage 5 CKD subjects, the maximum observed increases on Days 14 and 15 also occurred at 8 hours post-dose and were ~4.7-fold (Day 14) and ~6.2-fold (Day 15) the pre-dose value on those days, respectively. There was no evidence of EPO accumulation in either population.
L2321: ## Repeat Dose (14 days) in End-Stage Renal Disease Subjects on Peritoneal Dialysis (Study 200942)
L2322: **Study Title:** A repeat-dose, open-label study to assess the pharmacokinetics of daprodustat and metabolites in subjects with End-Stage Renal Disease undergoing peritoneal dialysis.
L2323: **Study Design:** This was a repeat dose, single arm study in End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) subjects undergoing peritoneal dialysis. Subjects received oral daprodustat at a dose of 5 mg once per day for 14 days. Serial blood samples were collected on Days 1 and 14 for PK and PD assessments, with additional pre-dose samples collected during the study. Dialysate PK samples were collected on Days 1, 14, and 15. Assessed PD markers included EPO and hepcidin.
L2324: Daprodustat was readily absorbed with a median time to maximum concentration (T_{max}) at 1- and 2-hours post-dose following single and repeat daprodustat doses, respectively. Daprodustat was rapidly eliminated from systemic circulation in ESRD subjects undergoing peritoneal dialysis with a t_{1/2} of approximately 2 hours following single and repeat doses. Daprodustat did not accumulate in plasma (geometric least squares [GLS] mean ratio: 0.896) and exhibited time-independent PK following repeat daprodustat doses in ESRD subjects.
L2325: Daprodustat metabolites appeared slowly in plasma with the median t_{max} ranging from 3 to 9 hours post-dose, and the t_{1/2} of daprodustat metabolites ranged from 3 to 27 hours following repeat daprodustat doses. All daprodustat metabolites were at steady-state concentrations following 14 days of oral daprodustat doses in ESRD subjects. Following 14 days of daprodustat doses, all the daprodustat metabolites appeared to accumulate in plasma, except for M4 (GLS mean ratio range: 1.02 [M4] to 1.95 [M13]). M2, M3, and M13 were the major circulating metabolites of daprodustat in the ESRD subjects, as defined by &gt;10% DRM in plasma. The results of the study showed no changes in protein binding at pre-dose, 3 hours, and 12 hours post-dosing for daprodustat, M4, and M5. Daprodustat was &gt;99% protein bound, and the 2 metabolites measured (M4 and M5) were approximately 69 to 76% protein bound in subjects undergoing peritoneal dialysis.

L2330: ## Pharmacodynamics
L2331: Baseline EPO concentrations were similar between continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD; 13.9 IU/L) and automated peritoneal dialysis (APD; 17.0 IU/L) subjects. EPO concentrations increased post-dose, reaching maximum levels at 8 to 12 hours post-dose, and then declined to pre-dose values by 24 hours. Maximal concentrations were 32.2 and 44.8 IU/L for the CAPD and APD subjects, respectively. For the ESRD subjects, EPO levels tended to be lower on Day 14 as compared to Day 1, and high variability in EPO concentrations was observed. Similar patterns were observed for CAPD and APD subjects.
L2332: ## **Food Effect in Healthy Subjects and Drug Interaction With a Strong CYP2C8 Inhibitor Gemfibrozil (Study PH113634)**
L2333: **Study Title:** Open-label study to assess the pharmacokinetics of daprodustat co-administered with a high-fat meal or an inhibitor of CYP2C8 (gemfibrozil).
L2334: **Study Design:** This was a single-center, open-label, single-sequence study in healthy subjects to assess the PK of oral daprodustat administered alone or co-administered with gemfibrozil (strong CYP2C8 inhibitor; oral). Subjects were administered 3 treatments: daprodustat 100 mg (fasted), daprodustat 100 mg (high-fat meal), and daprodustat 100 mg plus gemfibrozil 600 mg at steady state.
L2335: **Table 189. Study Design for PH113634**

L2338: ## **Results and Conclusions**
L2339: Twenty-three subjects were enrolled, and 21 subjects completed the study. Co-administration of a single 100 mg daprodustat dose with a high-fat, high-calorie meal resulted in an 11 and 31% decrease in daprodustat AUC(0-inf) and Cmax, respectively, and a 1 h mean delay of tmax relative to fasted administration. Similar t1/2 values were observed for the two prandial states. The 90% confidence interval (CI) of the adjusted geometric mean ratio was 0.84-1.01 for AUC(0-inf) and 0.61-0.82 for Cmax, concluding that a high-fat meal did not have a clinically significant effect on the AUC and Cmax of daprodustat. For daprodustat metabolites, slight increases in exposure (AUC(0-inf)) were observed when daprodustat was co-administered with food. The 90% CIs of AUC(0-inf) GLSM ratios for daprodustat metabolites ranged from 0.99 to 1.21.

L2346: Co-administration of a single 100 mg dose of daprodustat with a strong CYP2C8 inhibitor (gemfibrozil) resulted in a 3.9- and 18.6-fold increase in daprodustat Cmax and AUC(0-inf), respectively. This significant increase in both rate and extent of systemic exposure of daprodustat when co-administered with gemfibrozil is consistent with daprodustat being primarily metabolized by CYP2C8. The decrease in CYP2C8 metabolism of daprodustat is reflected by its ~4-fold increase in t½, 2.51 h to 9.26 h when co-administered with gemfibrozil. Tmax was also delayed from 1.00 to 4.00 h. The appearance of daprodustat metabolites was delayed by ~9-10 h as tmax shifted from 3-4 h for each metabolite to ~12 h when daprodustat was co-administered with gemfibrozil; the Cmax and AUC(0-inf) of metabolites were reduced by at least 90% and 67%, respectively.

L2357: ## Food Effect (CKD Meal) in Healthy Subjects (Study 207727 Part 2)
L2358: **Study Title:** A single center, single dose, open-label, randomized, 2-way crossover study in healthy Japanese male subjects to evaluate the bioequivalence of daprodustat tablets (2 mg tablet vs. 4 mg tablet) (Part 1) and the food effect on the pharmacokinetics of daprodustat (Part 2).
L2359: **Study Design:** The purpose of Part 2 of this study was to assess the effect of food on the single-dose PK of daprodustat in healthy Japanese male subjects administered the commercial tablet formulation.
L2360: Part 2 was a single-center, single dose, fed/fasted, open-label, randomized, 2-way crossover study in healthy Japanese male subjects. Subjects received a daprodustat 4 mg tablet (commercial formulation made by Process 1) 30 minutes after the end of a standard CKD meal (500-700 kcal, comprised of 12-16 g protein, 1 to 2 g salt, and up to 500 mg potassium) or in the fasted state. Following a washout period of 5 days, subjects crossed over to receive treatment in the opposite prandial state. Blood samples for PK analysis were collected prior to dosing and until 24 hours post-dose following each dose.
L2361: **Results and Conclusions:** Twelve subjects enrolled in Part 2 (food effect) of this study and all subjects completed the study. Following administration of daprodustat under fed and fasted conditions, similar daprodustat peak concentrations were observed though Tmax was reached 1 hour later in the fed state. There were no apparent differences in t1/2 between fed and fasted states. Metabolites were not analyzed in this study.

L2366: ## Single Ascending Dose Study in Healthy Adults (Study PHX111427)
L2367: **Study Title:** A Phase I, randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation study to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of single oral doses of GSK1278863A in healthy subjects.
L2368: **Study Design:** Study PHX111427 was a single-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-escalating, single dose, sequential parallel group study to investigate the safety, tolerability, PK and PD of GSK1278863A in healthy adult subjects. Subjects were dosed sequentially in six ascending dosing cohorts corresponding to six dose levels ranging from 2 mg to 300 mg of GSK1278863A. Within each cohort, a total of six subjects were randomized to receive a single, oral dose of daprodustat or placebo in a ratio of 2:1 (four active: two placebo). Thirty-six subjects were enrolled and completed the study.
L2369: ## Results and Conclusion
L2370: Daprodustat was readily absorbed following single dose administration with the median maximum concentration achieved between 1.25-2.00 hours post dose across different dose levels. Daprodustat was eliminated from systemic circulation rapidly with short terminal half-lives ranging from 0.8-4.0 hours across the dose range of 2 mg-300 mg.

L2382: ## Multiple Ascending Dose Study in Healthy Adults (Study PH112842)
L2383: **Study Title:** A Phase I, randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation study to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of repeat oral doses of GSK1278863A in healthy subjects.
L2384: **Study Design:** Subjects were dosed in 5 dosing cohorts corresponding to 4 once-daily regimens (15 to 100 mg) and one twice daily (BID) regimen (25 mg in the morning and evening). Dosing cohorts consisted of six subjects. Within each cohort, subjects were randomly assigned to receive either GSK1278863A or placebo in a 2:1 ratio (4 active:2 placebo). Each subject was dosed daily for up to 14 days.
L2385: ## Results and Conclusion
L2386: A total of 30 subjects were randomized to treatment (Figure 48). Of these, 29 completed the study, and one subject in Regimen D (25 mg BID) discontinued due to an adverse event. Daprodustat was absorbed with a median T_{max} range 1 to 4 hours and was eliminated from systemic circulation with t_{1/2} values ranging from 1.0 to 2.3 h. Daprodustat exposure (C_{max}, AUC) increased dose proportionally following daily doses up to 100 mg. Daprodustat did not significantly accumulate in plasma over 14 days of dosing, and steady-state plasma concentrations were achieved by Day 2.

L2406: ## 14.5.1. Summary of Applicant's Population PK Analysis
L2407: Population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) analysis was conducted using 3523 evaluable daprodustat concentrations and 573 below the limit of quantitation (BLQ) data in a total of 707 subjects, including five studies; one Phase 2B study (205665) and four Phase 3 studies (204837, 201410, 200807 and 200808). A brief overview of the studies is provided in Table 197. The dose used in the analysis included 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24 mg once daily (QD) and 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32 and 48 mg TIW. Summary statistics of the continuous and categorical covariates that were evaluated in the population PK analysis are shown in Table 198.

L2444: The Applicant claimed that a 3-compartment PopPK model with first-order elimination from the central compartment together with 5 absorption transit compartments, best described daprodustat PK. Allometric scaling was applied to all drug clearance (CL) and volume terms using fixed exponents (0.75 and 1.00 respectively) to account for PK variability related to body weight.
L2445: The final daprodustat PK model parameter estimates and the corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) from Bootstrap are presented in Table 200. The goodness-of-fit plots for the final daprodustat PK model are presented in Figure 49. The analysis plan included the Goodness-of-Fit (GoF) plots that use the normalized predicted distribution error (NPDE) instead of conditional weighted residuals (CWRES), as CWRES is not defined for BLQ observations, NPDE take the likelihood of the BLQ data into account and are, therefore, more appropriate for the M3 method that was used to model the PK data. Due to the use of the M3 method to incorporate the BLQ data, the prediction-corrected visual predictive check (VPC) could not be generated. The VPC based on all data from five studies (Figure 50) illustrated the prediction percentiles and corresponding 95% CI of simulated concentrations overlaid on the observed daprodustat concentrations and the corresponding 5th and 95th percentiles.

L2455: Covariate analysis showed only two significant covariates were identified: concomitant clopidogrel use reduced daprodustat clearance by 42.4%, and subjects that were non-dialysis dependent had a 45.6% higher k_a compared to dialysis dependent subjects. There are no significant covariate effects of age, body weight, sex, or hyporesponder status. Body weight, as a covariate, was implemented in the PopPK model as allometric exponents applied to CL and V model parameters. The simulated covariate effects on C_{max} and AUC from body weight, dialysis and Study 205665, and concomitant drug use relative to a reference subject (non-dialysis dependent, not using clopidogrel, body weight of 74.6 kg) are shown in Figure 51, Figure 52, and Table 201. Body weight, as a covariate, was implemented in the PopPK model as allometric exponents applied to CL and V model parameters. The AUC ratio for subjects weighing &gt;75 kg to ≤ 75 kg (estimate: 0.74, 90% CI: 0.68 – 0.80) and corresponding C_{max} ratio (estimate 0.68, 90% CI: 0.64 – 0.73) suggests these changes are unlikely to be clinically relevant given the individualized treatment modality of daprodustat in CKD.
L2456: Of note, the maximum daprodustat dose level in the current analysis dataset was 24 mg for the QD dose studies and 48 mg for the TIW dose study 204837. Additional simulations were performed with the final POPK model to calculate the exposure metrics for a typical dialysis patient (without concomitant clopidogrel use and 74.6 kg body weight) at the maximum daprodustat dose level and is shown in Table 202.

L2472: ## Reviewer's Comments
L2473: The Applicant's final population PK model as described above is adequate to describe the daprodustat serum concentration-time profiles of patients with CKD in studies 205665, 204837, 201410, 200807 and 20080, following the administration of daprodustat ranging from 1 mg to 48 mg QD. The shrinkage value was 14.6% for IIV on CL/F, 7.6% for IIV on k_a, and condition number was 12.8, indicating there was no obvious bias in the parameter estimates. Therefore, the PK model is acceptable for simulating post-hoc exposure metrics, e.g., C_{max} and C_{tau} of daprodustat for exposure-response (E-R) analyses.
L2474: Covariate analysis identified 2 statistically significant covariates: concomitant clopidogrel use reduced clearance by 42.4%, and subjects that were non-dialysis dependent had 45.6% higher k_a compared to dialysis dependent subjects. There are no significant covariate effects of age, body weight, sex, or hyporesponder status. The impact of the following intrinsic and extrinsic factors on the population pharmacokinetics of daprodustat in patients with CKD were quantified using simulations of typical subjects with the final model: dialysis (no change in AUC and -14% in C_{max}), and concomitant clopidogrel use (+74% AUC and +18% C_{max}).
L2475: However, a PopPK-based DDI evaluation for concomitant clopidogrel use can be limited due to the following reasons: inadequacy of sample size, lack of clear medication history prior to study entry, lack of dosing records for concomitant medications (e.g., dose level, dose frequency, formulation, route of administration, start and stop date and clock time, duration, dose modification, presence of other concomitant medications were not recorded), missing food, and/or other potential confounding factors, and inadequacy of PK sampling timepoints relative to concomitant medication dosing. In addition, the Applicant only used a binary covariate for concomitant clopidogrel use rather than a time varying covariate model.
L2476: In summary, the Applicant's current PopPK based DDI assessment is not adequate, which may significantly underestimate the true DDI effect due to the following reasons:
L2477: - The binary covariate analysis was performed in the Applicant's PopPK modeling without clear dosing history.
- Lack of adequate daprodustat PK samples during the elimination phase in clinical trials.
- Lack of medication history prior to study entry (that may have prolonged effects on drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination) and dosing records for concomitant medications: e.g., dose level, dose frequency, formulation, route of administration, start and stop date and clock time, duration, dose modification, in PopPK dataset.
L2478: The Applicant's justification based on efficacy/safety for minimum PK effect of clopidogrel and phosphate binders, iron, or acid reducing agents coadministration (use/no use) are also not acceptable. These can be confounded by dose titration to maintain target Hb range of 10 to 11.5 g/dL. Therefore, the Applicant's current PopPK based DDI assessments are not adequate.
L2479: To support TIW dosing for dialysis patients, PopPK simulations were performed. The results showed the weekly AUC is slightly higher with 24 mg QD compared to 48 mg TIW, corresponding to the higher weekly dose in the former (168 mg) compared to the latter (144 mg).
L2480: In summary, the PopPK model supports no dose adjustment for the above-mentioned specific populations such as age, gender, body weight, and non-dialysis dependent status but is not sensitive to evaluate drug interactions.
L2481: ## 14.5.2. Summary of Applicant's Population Dose response model
L2482: The initial daprodustat dose response analysis of Hb in anemic subjects with chronic kidney disease was developed in 2015 using 11,810 Hb observations in a total of 710 subjects. The structural model used to describe the time course of Hb was comprised of a precursor cell compartment, where the baseline production of precursors was a function of baseline Hb, and 12 transit compartments that described the RBC lifespan as shown in Figure 53.

L2499: ## Reviewer's Comments
L2500: The Applicant's final population dose Hb model developed in 2015 as described above is adequate to describe the Hb concentration time profiles of patients with CKD after treatment with placebo or daprodustat (0.5 to 25 mg QD). Model diagnostics and predictive performance of the model (as assessed by prediction and variability corrected predictive checks) were acceptable. Based on model simulations, the proposed starting doses, dose levels, and dose adjustment scheme appear to be appropriate and were predicted to lead to Hb levels within the target range of 10 to 11 g/dL, which was subsequently confirmed in phase 3 clinical trials.
L2501: ## 14.5.3. Summary of Applicant's Exposure-Response Analysis
L2502: ## 14.5.3.1. Longitudinal Exposure-Response Analysis to Quantify the Effect of Daprodustat on Hemoglobin Changes in Subjects With Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Dialysis From Studies 200807, 204837 and 204836
L2503: (b) (4) TIW dosing regimen versus QD in subjects with CKD undergoing dialysis, multivariate longitudinal population exposure-response analysis was conducted using three studies: 200807, 204837 and 204836. The initial daprodustat dose response Hb model in anemic subjects with CKD was developed in 2015 to support phase 3 dose selection (see details in section 14.5.2). The Applicant further updated their 2019 Dose-Hb model with longitudinal Hb data from study 204836 and data from three Japanese Phase 3 studies. Lastly, additional Hb data from 204837 and 200807 studies were used to further update their final 2022 Dose-Hb model. The above dose response models showed consistent parameters estimates and model predictive performance.
L2504: For the current longitudinal population concentration-Hb (Conc-Hb) model, the PK data from subgroup populations from the three studies (200807, 204837 and 204836) with corresponding Hb levels were pooled and analyzed using a population approach with evaluation of patient covariates on the model parameters.
L2505: Summary statistics of the continuous and categorical covariates that were evaluated in the E-R analysis are shown in Table 206.

L2550: ## **14.5.3.2. Summary of Applicant's Exposure-Response for Safety**
L2551: To support the proposed TIW dosing regimen with higher maximum concentration (C_{max}) in dialysis-dependent patients, the Applicant conducted multivariate E-R analyses using a logistic regression model and Cox proportional hazards regression model to quantify the relationship between daprodustat PK exposures (e.g., average C_{max} up to an event for patients with an event and average C_{max} during treatment for patients without an event) and safety measures
L2552: (thromboembolic event, nonfatal myocardial infarction (MI), and nonfatal hospitalization for HF) by Week 52 based on data from Studies 200807 and 204837.
L2553: For each PK Population subject in these two studies, the average cumulative dose (i.e., total dose for each subject divided by duration of dosing up to the time of the safety event or 52 weeks in those without a safety event) was calculated to obtain the average QD or TIW dose and the observed C_{max} from the corresponding PK Day dose was extrapolated to determine the C_{max} at the subject's estimated average QD or TIW dose. The extrapolated average C_{max} up to the time of the event was calculated as the observed C_{max} divided by the dose administered on the PK Day multiplied by average QD or TIW dose. Results are summarized in **Table 208**. For all safety endpoints, there was a small number of events. For MI and thromboembolic events, the confidence intervals for the hazard ratio (HR) and the odd ratio (OR) included one.

L2565: ## 14.6. Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Modeling Review
L2566: ## Executive Summary
L2567: The objective of this review is to evaluate the adequacy of the Applicant's PBPK report regarding evaluation of daprodustat's (GSK1278863) drug-drug interaction with a moderate CYP2C8 inhibitor clopidogrel using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling to support the intended uses. Specifically, the Applicant applied the PBPK modeling approach to assess the effects of clopidogrel on the exposure of daprodustat, following multiple dose administration of daprodustat. The Division of Pharmacometrics has reviewed the PBPK report, supporting modeling files, and the Applicant's responses to FDA's information request (IR) submitted on July 15, 2022, and concluded that the effects of clopidogrel on the PK profiles of daprodustat following multiple oral dose administration in healthy subjects were potentially underpredicted because the clopidogrel PBPK model was not reliably validated.
L2568: ## Background
L2569: Daprodustat, a HIF PHI, is proposed for the treatment of anemia due to chronic kidney disease in adults on dialysis and not on dialysis. The starting dose of daprodustat is based on the patient's dialysis status and hemoglobin level. For those switching from an erythropoiesis stimulating agent (ESA) to JESDUVROQ, the dose is based on their existing ESA dose. For details of the proposed dose regimen, please refer to the labeling of daprodustat. The dosage form of daprodustat is a tablet with different strengths (1 mg, 2 mg, 4 mg, 6 mg, and 8 mg).
L2570: Following oral administration, daprodustat is readily absorbed with median T_{max} in healthy subjects ranging from 1 to 4 hours. Daprodustat exhibited linear PK with generally dose-proportional increases in plasma exposure from 2 mg to 300 mg. The absolute bioavailability of daprodustat is 65%. Daprodustat has an approximately equal distribution between plasma and blood cells. Following intravenous dosing, the volume of distribution at steady state in healthy subjects is 14.3 L (Study 200232). Following oral or intravenous administration of radiolabeled daprodustat to healthy adults, approximately 40% of the total circulating radioactivity in plasma was daprodustat, and the remaining 60% was metabolites. Three metabolites each accounting for more than 10% of circulating drug-related material have been identified (Study 200942). Within seven days of an oral dose of radiolabeled daprodustat, 74% of the radioactivity was recovered in the feces, and 21% in the urine. Approximately 99.5% of the dose was excreted as oxidative metabolites, with the rest accounted for by daprodustat (Study 200232).
L2571: Daprodustat clearance was driven by cytochrome P450 (CYP) 2C8 metabolism (in vitro f_{m,CYP2C8} of ~96%, CD2010/00300/00) with a minor contribution by CYP3A4 metabolism and urinary excretion (2012N157420_01). Gemfibrozil, a strong CYP2C8 inhibitor, increased daprodustat AUC and C_{max} by 19- and 3.9-fold, respectively (Study PH1113634). Trimethoprim, a weak CYP2C8 inhibitor, increased AUC and C_{max} of daprodustat by 1.5 and 1.3-fold, respectively (Study 200229).
L2572: In vitro, daprodustat is not a competitive or time-dependent inhibitor of CYPs 1A2, 2A6, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, and 3A4. Daprodustat inhibited CYP2C8 with a calculated half-maximal inhibitory concentration IC_{50} value of 21\muM (study UH2008, CD2008). Daprodustat is not an in vitro inducer of CYP1A2, CYP2B6, or CYP3A4 (study CD2008). Daprodustat is a BCRP substrate in vitro but not a substrate of human drug transporters P-gp, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OATP2B1 OCT1, OAT1, OAT3, OCT2, MATE1, or MATE2-K. Daprodustat is not an inhibitor of transporters P-gp, BCRP, OAT1, OAT3, OCT2, MATE1 and MATE2-K in vitro. Daprodustat is an in vitro inhibitor of human OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 (study UH2008, CD2008).
L2573: ## Methods
L2574: ## PBPK Software
L2575: Simcyp v20 (Certara, UK) was used by the Applicant to develop the daprodustat PBPK models and predict the PK of daprodustat with and without CYP2C8 modulators. The reviewer used the same software and version for analyses.
L2576: ## Model Development
L2577: During PBPK model development, the ADAM module in Simcyp was used to investigate the mechanistic drug absorption and dissolution profiles. A minimal PBPK model was employed to understand the tissue distribution of daprodustat. The final input parameters for daprodustat are summarized in Table 209.

L2582: ## Population, Victim, and Perpetrator Drug Models
L2583: The Simcyp software built-in virtual healthy volunteer population and clinically relevant probes substrates, inhibitors or inducers have been utilized. The default PBPK models of gemfibrozil and trimethoprim in Simcyp were used for DDI prediction. The PBPK models of clopidogrel and its glucuronide were developed based on published data (Tornio et al. 2014; Shebley et al. 2017; Varma et al. 2019). Simcyp built-in models of repaglinide and the PBPK models of pioglitazone and montelukast built by the Applicant based on were used to qualify the ability of the clopidogrel PBPK model to simulate DDIs with CYP2C8 substrates as well as a CYP3A4 substrate. No modifications were made to the original models.
L2584: ## PBPK Simulation Trial Design
L2585: Simulations for daprodustat PBPK qualification and verification used a fixed study population, where individual subject data were available to match the observed clinical PK. Simulations were designed to replicate the situation in the actual daprodustat clinical studies, with either the exact number of subjects or sufficient subject numbers, sex, proportion of males and females in appropriate virtual populations of healthy volunteer subjects in replicate N trials to have a representative total of at least 100 subjects or more. Where individually matched patient demographic data and PK information were not available (e.g., model application), simulations were conducted using the default ranges within the Simcyp simulator (v20).
L2586: ## Model Refinement and Validation
L2587: - The PBPK model was validated against the adult PK studies following a single intravenous dose of 0.05 mg (study 200232), single oral doses of 2 mg, 5 mg, and 15 mg (study PHX111427) and repeated (QD) oral doses of 5 mg, 15 mg, and 100 mg (studies PHI112842, PHI116008 and PHI115573) daprodustat in healthy subjects.
- The PBPK model was optimized and validated with DDI studies in adult healthy subjects treated with gemfibrozil (study PHI113634) and trimethoprim (study 200229) respectively.
L2588: ## Model Application
L2589: The daprodustat PBPK model was applied to perform prospective drug-drug risk assessment as a victim after coadministration of clopidogrel
L2590: ## FDA's Assessment
L2591: - As stated in the PBPK report by the Applicant that 'the clopidogrel PBPK base model was developed in Simcyp based on published data (Tornio et al. 2014; Shebley et al. 2017; Varma et al. 2019). An information request was issued requesting the Applicant to provide evidence that the cited models of clopidogrel and its glucuronide could simulate the plasma concentration-time profiles and predict the magnitude of interaction observed in drug interaction studies using Simcyp simulator version 20.
- In the PBPK report, PBPK models of pioglitazone and montelukast used to qualify the clopidogrel models are currently not available in Simcyp v20. An information request was issued requesting the Applicant to submit the full documentation of model development and model verification for pioglitazone and montelukast using the Simcyp V20, including comparison of predicted and observed PK profiles, PK parameters and DDIs with CYP inhibitors.
L2592: ## Applicant's Response to FDA's IR and FDA's Assessment
L2593: In the response to our IR, the Applicant provided additional details and verification regarding the clopidogrel and clopidogrel-glucuronide Simcyp v20 PBPK models used in PBPK report (2019N396674). Briefly, the Applicant compared the simulated PK parameter values with those observed clinical data extracted from a variety of clinical studies for both clopidogrel and clopidogrel glucuronide. As shown in Table 210, the PK parameters of clopidogrel-glucuronide,
L2594: the major driving force for CYP2C8 inhibition, were significantly underpredicted compared with the observed clinical data for several studies. These discrepancies might be potentially explained by between-study variability; as shown in Figure 59, a majority of the observed concentrations fell between the 5th and 95th of the prediction confidence intervals. The ability of the clopidogrel models to predict their interactions with CYP2C8 substrates will be discussed in the Results section.
L2595: The Applicant developed PBPK models of pioglitazone and montelukast based on references and verified these models by comparing the simulated PK profiles and parameters with available clinical literature reports after both IV and oral dosing routes. The results demonstrated that the montelukast model could simulate the plasma PK profiles of montelukast reasonably well but the pioglitazone model significantly overpredicted the clearance of pioglitazone following IV administration (Table 211) and underpredicted pioglitazone AUC following oral administration of multiple doses of 30 mg pioglitazone (Table 212). However, both montelukast and pioglitazone models could predict the effects of gemfibrozil on their exposure (Table 213).

L2617: ## Can Daprodustat PBPK Model Reasonably Describe the PK of Daprodustat?
L2618: Yes, PBPK simulations reasonably predicted the PK profiles of daprodustat following a single intravenous dose of 0.05 mg, single oral doses of 2 mg, 5 mg, and 15 mg and multiple (QD) oral doses of 5 mg, 15 mg, and 100 mg of daprodustat in healthy subjects, as demonstrated in Figure 60 and by a reasonable agreement between predicted and observed values for AUC and Cmax in Table 214.

L2627: ## Can Daprodustat PBPK Model Reasonably Describe the Effects of Gemfibrozil and Trimethoprim on the PK of Daprodustat in Healthy Subjects?
L2628: Yes, the contribution of the CYP2C8 pathway to daprodustat clearance (e.g., assumption of fm,CYP2C8) was verified and calibrated using clinical DDI data with gemfibrozil. Briefly, an in vitro study using human liver microsomes attributed approximately 96% metabolism to CYP2C8. Using this value as fm,CYP2C8 to determine recombinant CLint values resulted in significant underprediction of the magnitude of DDI with gemfibrozil (predicted AUC ratio of 12-fold versus observed 18.6-fold). The Applicant optimized the fm,CYP2C8 value to 98.1% so that the predicted AUC ratio (15.1-fold) was within 20% of the observed AUC ratio (Table 215). The simulated and observed daprodustat plasma concentration-time profiles in the presence and absence of gemfibrozil are shown in Figure 61. Notably, the increase in contribution via CYP2C8 resulted in overprediction of DDI effect of trimethoprim (200 mg BID) on daprodustat (Table 215). However, the optimized fm,CYP2C8 value is still acceptable, as it may give a conservative estimate of the effect of clopidogrel on daprodustat DDI.

L2637: ## Can Daprodustat PBPK Model Predict the Effects of Clopidogrel on the PK of Daprodustat Following Multiple Oral Dose Administration in Healthy Subjects?
L2638: The magnitude of interaction between clopidogrel and daprodustat may potentially be underpredicted because the current clopidogrel PBPK model was not reliably validated. As stated in the previous sections, the observed PK profiles of both clopidogrel and clopidogrel-glucuronide could not be consistently reproduced by the PBPK models of clopidogrel and its glucuronide (Table 210). Furthermore, these clopidogrel PBPK models significantly underpredicted repaglinide DDI as indicated in Table 216, even though the predicted clopidogrel and its glucuronide exposure was consistent with that observed in the study (Table 210) and the repaglinide PBPK model was verified (data not shown). These findings suggest that these clopidogrel PBPK models were not well validated and cannot be used confidently to predict the DDI of daprodustat co-administered with clopidogrel.
L2639: To further evaluate the potential interaction between clopidogrel and daprodustat, the clinically observed interactions of known CYP2C8 substrates with gemfibrozil or clopidogrel were compared (Table 217). Based on the relative difference in the magnitude of interaction of CYP2C8 substrates with clopidogrel and gemfibrozil, the PBPK model-predicted interaction with clopidogrel following a single 300-mg clopidogrel approximated to the lower bound of the values estimated from the clinical DDI data. Following steady state clopidogrel, there was less data available to evaluate the model prediction. However, based on the results from the interaction between repaglinide and clopidogrel, the interaction was expected to be similar to that observed following a single 300-mg dose of clopidogrel. In addition, because daprodustat is the most sensitive CYP2C8 substrate, increase in its AUC is expected to be greater compared to that observed from repaglinide following the same clopidogrel treatment regimen. Therefore, there is a potential that the interaction between daprodustat and clopidogrel following steady state clopidogrel was underpredicted by the PBPK modeling approach. Taken together, the current clopidogrel PBPK model was not reliably validated and the effects of clopidogrel on the PK of daprodustat following multiple oral dose administration in healthy subjects may be underpredicted.
